title: control server: bound request lines and concurrent connections
author: SteamSmith
body:
## Summary

`apps/soundcraft/src/control_server.rs` (the opt-in `--control` loopback channel) read request lines with `BufRead::lines`, which buffers an entire line before anything checks its size, and spawned one thread per accepted connection with no limit.

- **Bounded line reads:** each line is read with `take(MAX_LINE + 1).read_until(b'\n', …)`. A line longer than `MAX_LINE` = 256 MiB (generous, since requests can carry documents or media as base64) gets an error reply and the connection is closed, without buffering the rest. Previously there was no line limit at all.
- **Connection cap:** at most `MAX_CONNECTIONS` = 16 connections are served at once; further ones get `{"ok": false, "error": "too many control connections"}` and are closed. A slot is released when its connection ends, including if its thread can't start or panics (`Drop` guard).

Everything else in request handling is unchanged (blank lines skipped, same replies, same timeouts). The approach mirrors DesignCraft's control server.

## Tests

New tests in `control_server.rs`:
- `lines_are_read_up_to_the_limit`: line at the limit accepted, CRLF stripped, final line without newline read, then end of stream
- `an_overlong_line_is_refused_without_reading_the_rest`: at most limit+1 bytes buffered, remainder left unread
- `requests_are_answered_with_their_ids`: end to end over a loopback socket with a stand-in UI
- `extra_connections_are_refused`: the 17th concurrent connection gets the error line

## How this was verified

On my Windows machine, Smart App Control blocks a dependency's build script (`parking_lot_core`), so I couldn't build the full app locally. Instead I compiled **this exact file**, unmodified, as a module of a small harness crate with stand-ins for `egui::Context` and `ControlRequest`. All four new tests pass there, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings -D clippy::unwrap_used -D clippy::expect_used -D clippy::panic` is clean on it. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes in the repo. title: Plugin scanning that can't crash the app: helper processes, off the UI thread, cached; plus IMessage for iZotope plugins
author: woodgrain816
body:
On a Windows machine with ~700 VST3 plug-ins, SoundCraft could not get through a plug-in scan, and a session using iZotope plug-ins could not be opened. This PR fixes both, in line with the **Never crash** rule, and with `docs/plugin-parity.md`'s note that out-of-process hosting would beat Pro Tools.

## What was happening (measured, Windows 11, SoundCraft 0.5.0)

- **The scan ran in the app, on the UI thread.** The window showed *Not Responding* for 6+ minutes and grew to 2.1 GB of loaded modules.
- **Licence dialogs stalled the scan.** iLok and activation windows from AVOX and Soundtoys plug-ins held it for as long as they stayed open.
- **One bad plug-in killed the app.** The scan then aborted with `fatal runtime error: Rust cannot catch foreign exceptions`, or an access violation in `iZotope\Insight 2.vst3` or `AVOX ARTICULATOR x64.vst3`. The same plug-ins load fine on their own. They crash only with hundreds of others loaded in the same process.
- **Opening a session that used a VST3 ran that whole scan first**, so opening a converted session hung, then crashed.
- **Every iZotope plug-in tried crashed on insert** (Ozone 11, Ozone 11 Equalizer, Neutron 4). Each calls `IHostApplication::createInstance` for an `IMessage` while it is being set up, and the host returned null.

## Changes (4 commits, rebased onto main at c0cb993)

1. **Log each plug-in file before loading it.** The in-process path now names the culprit as the log's last line. It also warns on files that take 5 s or more, and logs a per-scan summary.
2. **`contributors/people.toml`**: my own entry.
3. **Scan in helper processes, off the UI thread, cached on disk.**
   - The app runs a copy of itself per file (`--plugin-scan-worker vst3|clap <path>`, handled first thing in `main`), up to 8 at a time, and reads one marked result line.
   - A helper that crashes, aborts or hangs (120 s timeout) costs only that file. It is logged by name, with the exit code decoded (access violation, fail-fast and so on).…

- Offscreen render (`ui_shot`) at 1600px looks unchanged; at 700px the toolbar is scrollable instead of clipped.
- `cargo fmt -p soundcraft-ui-egui --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui --test shared_controls --test shortcuts` — all pass

title: fix(dsp): a huge finite sample rate is no pitch, not an overflow (#241)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #241.

With a sample rate like `1e30`, the shortest lag in `yin` saturates to `usize::MAX` and `min_tau + 2` overflows. `audio_to_notes` goes through `yin`, so both panicked. The check is now `min_tau.saturating_add(2)`, so an impossible lag range ends in the `None` ("no pitch") the function already returns for frames it can't analyse.

Validation:
- two unit tests next to `silence_and_garbage` (`yin` at 1e30 and `f32::MAX`, `audio_to_notes` at 1e30) panic with "attempt to add with overflow" on main and pass here
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-dsp` passes
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-dsp --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(track): vca: null clears a VCA assignment, as documented (#237)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #237.

`track.vca` documents `vca: null` as "no VCA", but it passed the value to `track_param`, which rejects `null` ("must be a track id or name"). Only an absent key cleared the assignment. `track.vca` now treats an explicit `null` as absent, the same way `plugin_state` does. `track_param` is unchanged, because the other commands that use it keep rejecting `null`.

Validation:
- new test `cmd::track::tests::vca_null_clears_the_assignment`:
  - `null` clears the assignment, and undo restores it;
  - `true`, an unknown id, an unknown name and a non-VCA track are still errors and leave the assignment alone.
  - It fails on main with `BadParams("track.vca", "`vca` must be a track id or name")`.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine` passes, `hostile_params` included.
- clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(control): apply the engine.commands filter to UI commands (#255)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #255.

`engine.commands {filter}` filtered the engine's rows, but the control handler then appended all 64 `UI_COMMANDS` rows unfiltered. So `filter: "zzzznomatch"` still returned every `window.*` / `ui.*` command. The UI rows now go through the same predicate as the engine (id or label substring, ASCII case-insensitive). The engine's predicate is a closure inside `cmd!`, so it's mirrored in `control.rs` with a comment pointing back to it. An absent or empty filter still lists everything.

Validation:
- `tests/commands_filter.rs` (the file the issue proposes): a filter matching one UI id, a label-only match, mixed case, and no match. It fails on main with all 64 UI rows. Dropping the label match or the lowercasing each fail a case.
- `absent_or_empty_filter_lists_every_ui_command` guards the other direction.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(window): keep the MIDI Editor open on Bring to Front (#254)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #254.

`window.midi_editor` and `window.midi_front` shared one arm that toggled `show_midi_editor`. So Window › MIDI Editor › Bring to Front closed an editor that was already open. `window.midi_front` now shows it and returns `{"value": true}`, like `window.workspace_front`. `window.midi_editor` still toggles.

Validation:
- `tests/midi_front_visibility.rs` (the file the issue proposes) goes through the real menu path (`command_for_path` + `invoke_menu`). Bring to Front twice keeps the editor open, and Bring to Front shows a closed editor. It fails on main with "Bring to Front hid the editor".
- `the_midi_editor_command_still_toggles` catches the opposite mistake.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

The `window.close | window.hide_floating` arm that #216 touches is left alone.

title: fix(midi-editor): a selected video clip is not a MIDI target (#258)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #258.

The MIDI editors find their clip with `!c.is_audio()`, which a video clip also passes. Selecting a video clip made it the "MIDI" target, so the editor went empty, and the Event List and MIDI Keyboard pointed at it too. The check is now `matches!(c.content, ClipContent::Midi { .. })`. All three callers (`score_editor.rs`, and the Event List and MIDI Keyboard in `windows.rs`) only ever want a MIDI clip.

Validation:
- `a_selected_video_clip_is_not_a_midi_target` in `tests/midi_panel.rs` covers two selections. A lone video clip gives no target; on main it gives `Some(ClipId(..))`. With `[video, midi]` selected, the MIDI clip is the target, which rules out a fix that just stops at the first non-MIDI clip.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(video-universe): filmstrip thumbnails use the clip's own movie time (#225)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #225.

In the Video Universe filmstrip, `(x - r.min.x) / r.width() * end` is already the timeline position, but the code added `c.start` again (minus `c.start.min(0)`). So for a clip after zero every thumbnail came from `2 × start` into the movie. For clips at or before zero that extra term cancelled out, which is why it only showed up for later clips.

The computation moved into a small pure `strip_position()` that leaves the clip start out of the sum. Results for clips at or before zero are unchanged.

Validation:
- `strip_position_is_the_timeline_position_for_clips_after_zero` fails with the old formula (`96000` vs `48000`) and passes here.
- `strip_position_is_unchanged_for_clips_at_or_before_zero` pins the old behaviour, including the clamp to the clip start.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(window): Hide All Floating Windows also hides Automation (#253)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #253.

Window › Hide All Floating Windows cleared Transport, Big Counter, Memory Locations, Undo History, Session Info and Audio Health, but not Automation. One line adds `show_automation = false` to the same arm. I checked with `git merge-tree` that it merges cleanly with #216, which splits that arm.

Validation:
- `tests/hide_floating.rs` (the issue's test) fails on main with "Automation must be hidden" and passes here.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

Other floating windows (Color Palette, Disk Usage, Task Manager, Metadata…) also stay open. The issue only asks about Automation, so I left them; happy to add them if you want Hide All to cover every one.

title: fix(edit-window): Pencil clicks on plugin lanes use the plugin's range (#224)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #224.

A Pencil click on a plugin automation lane took its value range from `param.range()`, which for plugin parameters is the generic `(f32::MIN, f32::MAX)`. So the click produced no usable value ("bad parameters for automation.set_point: value required") and no point was added. Dragging already uses `plugin_range(track, &param)`; the click now does too.

Validation:
- `a_pencil_click_on_a_plugin_lane_uses_the_plugin_range` (kittest, demo session, Kick's `plugin:a:input_gain` lane) clicks a quarter of the way down the lane and expects one point at −12 dB. On main it adds no point and shows the issue's error.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

The range lookup now appears in three places (draw, drag, click). I didn't pull it into a helper, to keep this small next to #209 and #216.

title: fix(midi-editor): Quantize snaps to the grid the editor shows (#226)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #226.

The MIDI editor's Quantize button always sent `"grid": "1/16"`, whatever grid the editor showed. `grid_ticks` was only computed after the toolbar was drawn. It's now computed first and passed as a number, which `event.rs`'s `grid_ticks` accepts (clamped to 1..15360 ticks).

Validation:
- `tests/midi_quantize.rs` clicks the real "Quantize" button. `quantize_follows_a_quarter_note_grid` gets 240 instead of 0 on main and passes here. `quantize_follows_a_sixteenth_note_grid` also passes on main: it only shows the click lands and 1/16 is unchanged.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

This moves a block that #137 also edits nearby, so one of the two will need a small rebase.

title: fix(eq): switches and choices redesign the filter on a running EQ (#239)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #239.

On a running EQ, `update()` snapped switch and choice parameters (HPF/LPF on, filter types…) into the smoothers. But `process` only redesigned the filters while a continuous smoother was still settling, so a switch flipped mid-playback didn't take effect. `update()` now calls `redesign()` when a snapped value changes. It doesn't allocate, so it's fine on the audio thread.

Validation:
- `eq_switches_and_choices_apply_to_a_running_eq` in `tests/plugins.rs` covers the issue's 7 cases, Channel Strip included. Each compares the instance changed while running with one built fresh with the new setting, within 0.1 dB. A guard checks that the two settings differ by more than 3 dB, so the comparison means something. On main all 7 fail with the issue's numbers (e.g. `eq_7band hpf_on=1: live -9.03 dB, fresh -33.28 dB`).
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-dsp` passes, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(video): H.264 parameter sets check their arithmetic before range checks (#251, #252)
author: marcoarnulfo

title: fix(markers): markers.edit applies the documented name (#236)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #236.

`markers.edit` documents `name` as the new name, but `edit_marker` only read `rename` (the key the Memory Locations panel sends), so `{"id": 1, "name": "Chorus"}` returned `{}` and changed nothing. It now takes `rename` first and falls back to `name`. When `name` is the selector (no `id` or `number`), the location already has that name, so nothing changes there. `color` is also documented and still ignored; I left it out of this PR.

Validation:
- `edit_marker_renames_with_documented_name` in `cmd/event.rs` renames one location by `id` and the other by `number`, checks the other location keeps its name, and checks that selecting by `name` still works. On main it fails with `("Verse", "Outro")` instead of `("Chorus", "Outro")`.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::event` and `--test hostile_params` pass, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(clip): Elastic Properties stretches the clip by the requested ratio (#227)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #227.

`elastic` set `stretch = ratio` on the clip it passed to `render_stretched`. That helper reads `length / stretch` source samples and stretches them to `out_len = length * ratio`, so the ratio was applied twice. At ratio 2 it rendered only the first half of the clip, stretched 4x, which is how a clip that is silent then tone came out all silent. At 0.5 it read past the clip's end, and at 4 and 0.2 it asked for 16 and 0.04 and was rejected. The clip handed to the renderer is now the unwarped base clip as it plays, the same way `edit.tce_to_timeline` and `clip.remove_pitch_shift` call the helper. `render_stretched` and its other callers are unchanged.

Validation:
- New `elastic_properties_stretches_the_clip_material` in `cmd/clip.rs` uses a synthetic mono source. At ratio 2, a clip that is silent then tone keeps the tone. At ratio 0.5, a silent clip on a longer source stays silent. Ratios 4 and 0.2 give 80,000 and 4,000 samples. On main each of the three parts fails separately: "the tone in the second half was lost", "audio from past the clip end leaked in", and `stretch ratio 16.000 is outside 0.1..10`.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib` for `cmd::clip`, `cmd::clip_more` and `tce_fits_timeline` passes, including the existing `elastic_warp_renders_and_remove_warp_restores`. Clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(dsp): pitch_shift reaches ±48 semitones (#243)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #243.

`pitch_shift` accepts ±48 semitones but hands the whole factor to `time_stretch`, which clamps to 0.1..=10. Anything past about +39.9 or -39.9 semitones came out as a 10x (or 0.1x) shift, so +48 gave 4400 Hz from a 440 Hz tone instead of 7040. When the factor is outside that range, it is now split into two `time_stretch` passes by its square root (4 and 4 for +48, 0.25 and 0.25 for -48). Factors inside the range still take the single pass, so ±24 and everything AudioSuite sends is unchanged.

Validation:
- New `pitch_shift_reaches_the_ends_of_its_range` in `tests/offline_meters.rs` shifts a 440 Hz sine by +40, +48, -40 and -48 and checks the frequency within 0.2%. On main, +40 measures 4400.0 Hz instead of 4434.9. If only the upward case is split, -40 measures 44.0 Hz instead of 43.65. With the fix, +48 measures 7040.0 Hz and -48 measures 27.48 Hz.
- The existing +12 and -7 checks (`pitch_shift_preserves_length_and_shifts`) and the rest of `offline_meters` pass, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(dsp): chorus and flanger tails follow their feedback (#242)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #242.

`ModFx::tail_samples` reported a fixed 200 ms for chorus and flanger, whatever the feedback. With chorus at 30 ms / 90% the echoes stay above -60 dB for about two seconds, so `apply_plugin_with_tail` cut them off. The tail now works like the delay plugin's: the number of repeats for the feedback to fall by 60 dB, times the longest delay in the sweep (base delay plus up to 6 ms of depth for chorus, base delay for flanger). It uses the absolute feedback because the flanger allows negative values, and it never goes below the old 200 ms. It's plain arithmetic on the parameters, with no allocation.

Validation:
- New `modulation_tail_covers_feedback_echoes` in `tests/plugins.rs` sends an impulse through chorus (30 ms, 90%) and flanger (10 ms, +95% and -95%), renders 5 s, and checks that the last sample above -60 dB falls inside `tail_samples()`. On main it fails with `chorus feedback 90: echo at 95039, tail 9600`. Without the `abs()` the -95% flanger case fails (`echo at 64799, tail 9600`).
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-dsp --test plugins` and `--test offline_meters` pass, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(midi-editor): Backspace in a text field leaves the selected notes alone (#223)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #223.

The MIDI editor's Delete/Backspace check read the key from the global input with no focus guard. The editor is drawn before dialogs, so with notes selected, pressing Backspace in the Rename Track field also ran `midi.note_delete`. The check now skips when `egui_wants_keyboard_input()` is true, the same guard the select-all and arrow keys a few lines above already use.

Validation:
- New `tests/midi_editor_keys.rs` selects two notes of the Keys clip with the Rename Track dialog open. It presses Backspace, then Delete, and checks that the name field took the key and the session is unchanged. On main it fails with "Backspace edited the session". A second test checks that both keys still delete the selected notes when no text field has focus.
- `midi_panel`, `rename_dialog` and `shortcuts` still pass, and clippy and fmt are clean (macOS, Apple silicon).

title: fix(edit): cut clip gain keeps the removed gain for paste (#230)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #230.

Cut Special > Clip Gain went through the same `reset_clip_gain` as Clear Special, so it zeroed the selected clips' gain but never filled the clip-gain clipboard: Paste Clip Gain then either had nothing to paste or pasted whatever was copied before. The cut now runs `copy_clip_gain` over the selection first and then resets, so it behaves like Copy followed by Clear in a single undo step. Clear Special is unchanged.

Validation:
- New `cut_clip_gain_can_be_pasted` test: cuts a -6 dB clip with an older -12 dB copy already in the clipboard, checks the source is back at 0 dB and that the paste applies -6 dB. Fails on main (pastes -12 dB), passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib clip_gain` and `--lib cmd::edit`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(track): Clear Trim Automation removes the trim lane (#233)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #233.

`track.clear_trim_automation` was registered with a handler that returned `{}` and did nothing, so the trim written by Trim Automation Write stayed in the session and in the render. It now removes the trim lane (`plugin:255:trim`, the same `trim_param()` that `track.coalesce_trim` drops) from the selected or explicitly named tracks, as one undoable edit, and returns how many tracks it cleared. Volume automation and other tracks are left alone.

Validation:
- New `clear_trim_automation_removes_only_trim` test: clears the selected track, then an explicit one, checks the other track's trim and the volume lane survive and that undo brings the trim back. Fails on main, passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib track`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(edit): Shuffle Clear moves automation with the clips (#232)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #232.

`edit.clear` rippled later clips left in Shuffle mode but never touched automation, so with Automation Follows Edit on the volume points stayed at their old positions while Cut, on the same range, moved them. Clear now does what Cut already does after removing the clips: when Automation Follows Edit is on it clears the lane points inside the range and, in Shuffle, shifts the later points left by the range length. With the option off nothing changes.

Validation:
- New `shuffle_clear_moves_automation_like_cut` test: Shuffle Clear over [4000, 6000) gives volume points at 0, 7000, 18000, the same result as Cut, and leaves them untouched with the option off. Fails on main, passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::edit`, `--test random_edits`, `--test hostile_params`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

One behaviour change to be aware of: with Automation Follows Edit on, Clear in Slip mode now also clears the automation points inside the range, the way Cut already does. The issue's Slip control still passes (its fixture has no point inside the range).

title: fix(event): Constant tempo applies only over its range (#238)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #238.

`event.tempo_constant` shared the handler of `event.tempo`, which reads `at`/`start` and ignores `end`, so it only inserted one tempo change: later changes inside the range stayed active and the new tempo ran on past the end. Constant now works like the other Tempo Operations: it reads the range (explicit `start`/`end`, or the timeline selection), sets the BPM at the start, removes the tempo events strictly inside, and puts back at the end tick the tempo that was in effect there. Both ticks are captured before editing, since the new tempo moves the end in samples. With no range it still inserts a single change, as before.

Validation:
- New `tempo_constant_is_bounded_by_its_range` test: 100 BPM, a 140 BPM change inside [24000, 96000), Constant 90 over that range; checks 100 before, 90 at the start and in the middle, 140 again at the old end tick. Fails on main, passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::event` and `--lib tempo`, `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(edit): trims stop at the neighbouring clips instead of overlapping them (#228, #229)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #228, fixes #229.

`edit.trim_to_file_boundaries` and `edit.trim_to_fill_selection` extended a clip as far as its source allowed without looking at the other clips on the playlist, so extending across a neighbour left two unfaded clips playing the same region (the constant-source repros in both issues render at double level). Both commands now ask one helper, `trim_limits`, how far the clip may grow: no earlier than the end of the clip before it and no later than the start of the clip after it on the same playlist. I chose to stop at the neighbour rather than overwrite it because that is what the commands that grow an existing clip already do (`edit.paste_merge_midi` and MIDI step input cap the host clip at `next_start`), and because the Edit window's trim handle drag extends through `edit.trim_to_fill_selection`, where eating the next clip would be a surprising result of a drag. A clip with no neighbour still expands to its full source extent as before, and a crossfade the clip already has with a neighbour is kept instead of being trimmed back.

One note on #229: its restoration check expects A to reach its full source length (20,000 frames) by overwriting B. With this change A grows up to B's start (5,000 to 12,000) and B is left intact. If you'd rather have the overwrite semantics of placing a clip, it is a small change in the same helper and I'm happy to switch.

Validation:
- New unit tests in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs`: both commands with a neighbour on each side stop at the neighbours with the expected start, end and source offset; a clip with no neighbour expands fully; an existing crossfade overlap survives Trim to File Boundaries. The three neighbour tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::edit`, `--test random_edits`, `--test hostile_params`, `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui --lib edit_window`
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` (macO…

title: Open .m4b audiobook files like .m4a
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
A user on Discord asked whether SoundCraft can edit their M4B audiobooks without converting them to MP3 first.

M4B is the same MP4/AAC container as M4A, and the decoder already reads it: format detection looks at the `ftyp` box, not the file name, and symphonia's MP4 reader doesn't check the brand. But `.m4b` files never showed up, because the extension was missing from:

- the desktop Open dialog filter (`apps/soundcraft/src/main.rs`)
- the web file picker (`apps/soundcraft-web/src/web.rs`)
- the in-app file browser (`crates/ui-egui/src/windows.rs`)
- the extension fallback in `detect_by_ext` (`crates/audio-io/src/lib.rs`)

This adds `m4b` to all four, plus a test that an `.M4B` hint maps to AAC.

Saving back to M4B is out of scope; export stays WAV/AIFF/FLAC.

title: Apply the Feet+Frames reference to counters and typed positions
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #235.

`setup.current_feet_frames` stored the new origin in `feet_frames.start`, but nothing read it: `format_position` and `parse_position` always counted feet+frames from sample 0. They now take the feet+frames origin next to the timecode start, and two small helpers on `Session` (`format_position`, `parse_position`) pass both, so `session.format_time`, typed positions, the toolbar and big counters, the ruler and the memory locations all use the same reference. The callers that passed `s.timecode_start` by hand now go through those helpers.

Validation: `crates/engine/tests/current_feet_frames_position.rs` sets `12+08` at sample 48000 (30 fps, 48 kHz). On main it reads `1+14` there; here it reads `12+08`, `14+06` at 96000, and typing `feet_frames:14+06` lands back on 96000.

```
cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test current_feet_frames_position
cargo test -p soundcraft-time -- format:: feet_and_frames
cargo clippy -p soundcraft-time -p soundcraft-model -p soundcraft-engine -p soundcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

(macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(mix): pan automation reads the same in playback and bounce
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #244.

Track pan was read once per block, at the block's first sample, and held for the whole block. Bounces render in 1024-frame blocks and playback in callback-sized blocks (up to 512), so the same pan curve landed on different samples: with a -1 -> +1 move over the first 480 samples, the bounce stayed hard left until sample 1023 while playback switched at 512. Now pan automation is read on a fixed 64-sample grid aligned to the timeline, and the routing matrix is applied per grid segment, so any block size gives bit-identical output. Tracks without pan automation keep the single matrix per block. 64 is a trade-off between zipper steps and matrix rebuilds; happy to switch to a smaller step or a per-sample ramp if you prefer.

Volume/trim, send levels and plugin parameters are still sampled per block; I left them alone to keep this to the reported case.

Validation:
- `pan_automation_does_not_depend_on_the_block_size` (soundcraft-mix): fails on main (1024-frame bounce still hard left at sample 600: L 0.5, R 0), passes here; compares 1024 vs 512, 100 and 37-frame renders exactly
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-mix --lib -- pan surround bus send render aux insert`
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-mix --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Create MIDI clips with the Pencil, Consolidate and the MIDI Editor
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #282. An empty MIDI or instrument track had no way to get a clip from the UI, so notes couldn't be entered by hand. `midi.new_clip` existed, but nothing in the UI called it.

- The Pencil draws a MIDI clip on an empty part of a MIDI or instrument track: a click makes one bar, and a drag covers the bars it crosses. Clips start and end on barlines, as Pro Tools does for the MIDI clips it creates, and stop at the next clip instead of overwriting it.
- Consolidate (Option+Shift+3 on macOS, Alt+Shift+3 on Windows and Linux) now works on MIDI and instrument tracks. The selection becomes one clip, gaps included, and an empty selection gives an empty clip. Muted clips stay silent and notes are cut where their clip ended, so it sounds the same.
- With an empty MIDI or instrument track selected, a click in the MIDI Editor adds a clip at the insertion point.
- The new clip is selected, so the MIDI Editor shows it right away.

Tested: CI checks pass locally (685 tests, 7 of them new), apart from six VST3 tests that abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Reorder tracks by dragging them in the Tracks list
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #170. Dragging a track in the Tracks list did nothing. Pro Tools reorders tracks when their names are dragged there, and SoundCraft's Edit window name plates already could.

- Rows can be dragged up and down, and a line shows the gap where the track will land.
- The drop runs `track.move`, so it is one undo step.
- A click still selects the track.

Tested: CI checks pass locally (680 tests, 2 of them new), apart from six VST3 tests that abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Drag or type the tempo in the toolbar
author: grovebit
body:
Part of #189 (its first point). Clicking and dragging the toolbar tempo did nothing. It was painted text, so changing the tempo meant opening Tempo Operations or the tempo ruler.

- The tempo is now a drag value that looks the same until it's hovered. Drag it to change the tempo (hold Shift for steps ten times finer), or click it and type a value from 5 to 1000 BPM.
- It edits the tempo change in effect at the playhead, the one it shows, and leaves later tempo changes alone.
- A whole drag is one undo step.

title: Locate clears plugin and delay-compensation state
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #247.

A locate during playback moved the position and dropped pending output, but never reset the mix engine, so inserts kept their state across the jump: a 5 ms lookahead compressor played 240 frames from the old position and a reverb kept ringing. `Cmd::Locate` now calls `mix.reset()` like Play and Stop already do. On its own that still wasn't enough: `reset()` left the delay-compensation lines (`align`, `align_pre`, `out_extra`) full, and `DelayLine::set` only reallocates when the length changes, so a track aligned behind a latent one still emitted old audio. `reset()` now zeroes them in place (no allocation, no locks on the audio thread).

I put the reset on the transport's Locate rather than in `MixEngine::render`'s "pos != last_end" branch, because that branch also fires on every loop wrap, and flushing there would cut reverb tails and drop the compensated tail at each loop pass. Happy to switch if you'd rather have it in the engine.

Validation:
- `locate_while_playing_drops_the_old_position_audio` (playback, compressor with lookahead and room_reverb): fails on main (compressor audio after the locate), passes here
- `reset_clears_delay_compensation_history` (mix, unprocessed track aligned behind a compressor track): fails on main (old aligned audio after reset), passes here
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-mix -p soundcraft-playback --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Restore Last Selection brings back the previous selection
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #231.

`edit.restore_last_selection` just returned the current range, so nothing was ever remembered to restore. Now `Engine::execute` notes the selection a command replaced (range and tracks) whenever a successful command changes it, so every selection path is covered without touching each command. It lives on the `Engine` next to the clipboard rather than in the document, so selecting still leaves the session clean (`is_dirty`) and it isn't saved with the session; opening another session clears it. Restore swaps it back in, so pressing it twice returns to where you were. With nothing remembered the command is disabled instead of reporting success. I also made it `noundo` like `edit.select`, since a selection change isn't a document edit. Happy to switch either of those.

Validation:
- `cmd::edit::tests::restore_last_selection_swaps_back_to_the_previous_range_and_tracks`: fails on main (selection stays 7000..9000 instead of 1000..4000), passes here
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib cmd::edit` / `cmd::edit_more` / `cmd::file` / `cmd::view` / `merge_tests` / `dirty_tests`, `--test session_transport`, `--test random_edits`
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Apply MIDI track offsets when scheduling notes
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #234.

`event.midi_track_offsets` stored `midi.offset.<track>` in the edit values, but `schedule_notes` in the mix engine never read it, so the notes played where they always had. The scheduler now reads the track's offset once per block and looks that many samples back into the clips, so the track plays exactly as if its MIDI had been moved by the offset (later for positive values, earlier for negative ones). Offline bounce and realtime playback both go through `schedule_notes`, so both pick it up.

Validation: `crates/engine/tests/midi_offset.rs` renders one synth note, sets a 24000-sample offset, resets it to 0, then moves the clip by 24000 instead. On main the offset render is identical to the baseline; here it differs, a zero offset gives the baseline back, and it is sample-identical to the moved-clip render.

```
cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --test midi_offset
cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib rtp_and_offsets
cargo clippy -p soundcraft-mix -p soundcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

(macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Plugin safety: read plugin state off the audio thread, keep refused settings, contain NaN plugins
author: grovebit
body:
Third-party plugins could hurt a session in three ways: saves read their state on the audio thread, a plugin that refused its saved settings lost them at the next save, and one plugin putting out NaN silenced the whole mix.

- Saves, bounces and autosaves read plugin state on the UI thread, through a handle per CLAP, VST3 and AU instance (like the editor handles). The audio callback no longer calls `save_state`, and a stalled device no longer makes saves wait 2 s.
- A plugin that refuses its stored state keeps it in the session until its own editor is opened, instead of saving its defaults over it.
- The engine checks each insert's and instrument's output. A plugin that puts out NaN or infinity has that block silenced and is skipped until playback stops or starts, and the status line names it.

Tested: 687 tests pass, 9 of them new (state reads from another thread against the CLAP and VST3 fixtures and Apple's AULowpass; NaN from inserts, instruments and the master; refused states). fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass. Six VST3 tests are skipped because they abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Automation passes replace the automation they play over, in one undo step
author: grovebit
body:
A write pass only added points, so the old automation survived between them (a covered window, which runs one pass a second since #192, kept almost all of the old ride), and riding a fader during a pass made two undo steps a frame, so the history before the pass was gone within two seconds.

- `automation.set_point` takes an optional `from` and removes the points between `from` and `at` first. Each point of a pass gives the previous one, so it replaces everything since then, however far apart the passes run.
- Stop writes a last point where playback stopped. A locate, a restart or a loop wrap starts afresh, so a jump never erases what it skipped.
- While a pass can write, `Engine::hold_merge` puts every merged gesture into the pass's undo step, the fader that drives it included.
- A command ends a gesture only when it changes the document, so Stop doesn't split the pass it ends.

Tested: 5 new tests (removing any part of either fix fails one); fmt, clippy, 683 tests pass (6 VST3 tests skipped: they crash on plugins installed on this Mac), assets, layers, wasm; in the app, a Latch pass ridden for 90 frames wrote its points as one undo step.

title: MCP: confine file access with --automation-read-root and --automation-write-root
author: isaac-levine
body:
`soundcraft-cli mcp` gives the agent on the other end the same file access as the user running it. VectorCraft already has two flags for this, so this adds the same ones here with the same names and behaviour, and one client config works across the apps. It is the same change as storytold/wordcraft#798, storytold/gridcraft#480, storytold/deckcraft#247 and storytold/pdfcraft#1448.

    soundcraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root /work/project --automation-write-root /work/project/out

**How it works**

Every file a command reads has to be inside the read root and every file it writes inside the write root. The new `crates/engine/src/file_access.rs` holds the roots and the path logic: make the path absolute, follow symlinks (for a file that doesn't exist yet, resolve its nearest existing ancestor and require the rest to be plain names), then compare with the root by whole path components, so `/work2` is not inside `/work`. On Windows the comparison ignores case and device names like `CON` and `NUL` are refused. Refusals come back as ordinary tool errors with VectorCraft's wording, for example `automation path rejected: outside the read root /work/project: /etc/passwd`.

The checks sit in `crates/engine/src/io.rs`. `session.open`, `file.import_audio`, `file.import_midi`, `file.import_video`, `file.import_clip_groups`, `file.import_session_data`, `track.load_preset` and `mix.sampler_load` used to call `std::fs` themselves. They now go through `io::read_file` and `io::read_text`, and the writers (session save, bounce, stems, clip export, clip groups, `io::replace_file`, the `Audio Files/` and `Backups/` folders next to a saved session) go through `io::write_file`, `io::write_path` and `io::make_dir`. A test walks every file under `crates/engine/src` and fails if one other than `io.rs`, `file_access.rs` and the test files touches `std::fs`, `File::open`, `File::create`, `OpenOptions`, `canonicalize` or the `is_file`, `is_dir` and `exists` probes. No module needed to be skip…

title: JSFX effects and a ReaPack client (JSFX Browser)
author: Limestudio90
body:
## Summary

SoundCraft can now run **REAPER JS effects (JSFX)** as plugins and **install more of them from ReaPack repositories**.

- **`soundcraft-jsfx-host`** (new, L1): a from-scratch EEL2 interpreter (clean-room: no REAPER/WDL code) that exposes each `.jsfx` as a `soundcraft_dsp::Plugin`. title: Plugin editor windows on Windows (VST3 and embedded CLAP)
author: Limestudio90
body:
## Summary

Third-party plugin GUIs now open on **Windows**. Until now VST3 editors were hosted on macOS only (`VST3 editors are not hosted on this platform yet`) and CLAP plugins that offer only an embedded editor were refused everywhere.

- **VST3** (`soundcraft-vst3-host`): a Windows implementation of the existing `window` module (`kPlatformTypeHWND`). The view's child window lives in a top-level `HWND` owned by the app's active window (stays above it, no taskbar button), sized from `getSize`, resized on `IPlugFrame::resizeView`. Closing it only hides it; the editor link's `idle` then detaches the view and destroys the window, exactly like the macOS path.
- **CLAP** (`soundcraft-clap-host`): floating editors work as before. Plugins that only offer an embedded editor now get the same kind of host window on Windows: `create(api, false)` → `get_size` → `set_parent` (our `HWND`) → `show`. `request_resize` is recorded by the host callback and applied by the editor's `idle` on the main thread (window resize, then `set_size`); closing the window destroys the GUI, then the window. Other platforms still report embedded editors as unsupported.
- Both stay inside each crate's isolated `ffi.rs` (`unsafe` only there, a `// SAFETY:` comment on every block). New Windows-only dependency: `windows-sys` 0.61 (already in the lockfile through other crates). The main thread is the one Rust names `"main"`, where the app runs its message loop.

Also fixes two Windows-only problems that kept the VST3 tests from building/running there:
- the VST3 test fixture assigned `kDefaultActive` (an `i32` with MSVC's enum layout in the `vst3` bindings) to a `u32` field (`as _` now);
- an unused variable in a unix-only test failed `clippy -D warnings` on Windows.

## Testing (Windows 11, toolchain 1.95.0)

title: feat(groove): add an editable arithmetic pattern builder
author: IfritisZ
body:
Groove Builder creates an editable six-row step pattern on an instrument track using the existing Drum Synth. Open it from Track > New Groove, the New Tracks dialog, a generated clip's context menu/double-click, or Window > Groove Builder. Creation and each explicit Apply are one undo step; saved recipes reopen without regenerating notes.

The new generator distributes integer pulses around a step cycle, supports user-edited cells, direct eighth/sixteenth timing, swing, seeded timing/velocity spread, and an optional arithmetic ending. It uses no external performance data, captured MIDI, application screenshots, assets or algorithm-extraction output. The editor is a native SoundCraft step worksheet and its icon is drawn in `crates/ui-egui/src/icons.rs`. No binary files are added; the attribution table remains contiguous.

The crossfade-ordering fix and regression seed are now separate in #422 and are not included here.

- Generator properties: exact pulse counts across 1–32 steps and rotations, deterministic bounded notes, direct swing timing, independent lane variation, manual cells and row mutes.

title: Audio device settings (system, devices, rate, buffer) and opt-in ASIO
author: Limestudio90
body:
## Summary

Until now SoundCraft always opened the system's **default** output and input device, at the session rate, with the driver's default buffer (`setup.playback_engine` stored a device and buffer size that playback ignored, see G-01). This PR adds the audio device settings a DAW needs, in the spirit of REAPER's *Audio device settings* and Pro Tools' *Playback Engine*:

- **Setup › Playback Engine** (and Setup › Hardware) is now a settings panel: **audio system** (cpal host: WASAPI, ASIO, Core Audio, ALSA, JACK…), **output device**, **input device**, **sample rate** (rates the device accepts), **buffer size** (sizes inside the device's reported range), *Refresh devices*, *Apply*/*Revert*, and a live status line (device · rate · channels · buffer for output and input).
- The choice is **per machine**, not per session: it lives in the UI preferences (`UiState.audio`, saved in `ui.json`) and is used at startup. *Apply* reopens the devices keeping the transport position; it is refused while recording (it would lose the take). Plugin instances and open editors are recreated with the new player.
- **`ui.audio_device`** (UI command, so CLI/MCP/control channel too): `{list: true}` returns every system with its devices (channels, rates, buffer range); `{system?, output?, input?, sample_rate?, buffer_size?}` (`null` = default) sets and applies the choice; it always returns the config and the open device.
- **Robust fallbacks** (never-crash): an unplugged/unknown device, an unavailable system or an unsupported rate falls back to the default with a log warning; a buffer size the driver refuses is retried with the driver's default; only if nothing opens does the existing silent clock take over.
- **Integer devices**: output and input now accept f32, **32-bit and 16-bit integer** formats (best first), converting from/to the f32 mix through scratch buffers allocated when the stream is built, so the audio callbacks still never allocate. This is what most ASIO drivers need.

title: Make the Zoom Preset, Waveform Zoom and Clip Rating keys work; add Commands Focus 1–5 and N
author: grovebit
body:
Part of #186 (waveform zoom can't zoom back out, zoom presets have no keys, N does nothing). Three registry shortcuts are written as key families, `Cmd+Ctrl+1-5`, `Cmd+Alt+0-5` and `Cmd+Alt+[ / ]`, which the shortcut parser can't read. So they never fired, though the menus show them.

- The keyboard handler takes these keys itself, as it does F1–F4. Cmd+Option+[ and ] zoom the waveforms out and in, Cmd+Option+0–5 rate the selected clips, and Cmd+Ctrl+1–5 recall the zoom presets. Other digits do nothing.
- Waveform Zoom and Clip Rating work on Windows and Linux too, with Ctrl+Alt. Cmd+Ctrl+1–5 stays macOS-only, like the other Mac Control-key shortcuts.
- Commands Focus (the a-z button) gets Pro Tools' 1–5 for the zoom presets and N for Insertion Follows Playback, on every OS.

Tested: CI checks pass locally (681 tests, 3 of them new), apart from six VST3 tests that abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Mix in a separate window: Edit and Mix on screen at once
author: Limestudio90
body:
## Summary

SoundCraft had one main window showing either Edit or Mix (`MainWindow::Edit | Mix`), so the two could never be seen together. In Pro Tools they are separate windows and many users keep one per monitor. This PR adds that:

- **Window › Mix in Separate Window** (checkbox at the end of the Window menu; UI command `window.mix_separate`, also in the command palette). When on, the Mix window opens in **its own native window** (an egui immediate viewport titled "<session> — Mix") and the main window keeps Edit.
- **Window › Mix** and **Cmd/Ctrl+=** bring the Mix window to the front instead of switching the main window; the menu-bar title shows "Edit".
- **Closing** the Mix window puts Mix back into the main window (the option turns off).
- The choice is part of `UiState` (`mix_separate`), so it is kept with the preferences.
- Backends without multiple windows get egui's embedded fallback (a floating egui window).

The Mix window content is the existing `mix_window::show` (docking included), unchanged.

## Testing (Windows 11, toolchain 1.95.0)

- Over the control channel with the demo session: enabling the option opens a second native window "Midnight Groove — Mix" next to the Edit window; strips render and update; closing it (WM_CLOSE) removes the window and Mix returns to the main window.

title: Refuse renders too long to finish instead of cutting the audio short
author: grovebit
body:
Renders longer than one offline buffer holds (about 93 minutes of stereo at 48 kHz) were cut short without a word, and the shortened audio replaced the clip, went onto the committed track or into the exported file.

- Render Clip Gain, Clip Effects Render, AudioSuite, Commit and Export Clips check the length first and refuse with the limit in seconds, as Consolidate does in #212.
- AudioSuite counts what Time Stretch, Pitch Shift and Varispeed make, so a fourfold stretch is refused at a quarter of the limit.
- TCE, Elastic Properties and Remove Pitch Shift stop at what the offline stretch makes, which is less than an hour above 74 kHz.
- Export Clips checks every clip before it writes a file.

Tested: 3 new tests (removing any of the six checks fails one); fmt, clippy, 681 tests pass (6 VST3 tests skipped: they crash on plugins installed on this Mac), assets, layers, wasm; in the app, a 100-minute stereo import is refused by all five commands, with the limit in the status line.

title: mix: a newly adopted plugin instance replaces a matching one in its slot
author: Limestudio90
body:
## Problem

In realtime playback the UI thread creates third-party plugin instances and hands them to the audio thread (`MixEngine::adopt`); `sync` places them on the next render.

If a plugin is removed and re-added in the same slot (same id, same channel count) and both session updates reach the audio thread in one `drain`, `sync` only sees the final session. The slot looks unchanged, so the old instance stays, and the new one is retired as an unclaimed leftover. The UI-side editor handle belongs to the new instance, which has now been destroyed. Opening the editor then fails with **"the plugin is gone"**, while the old instance keeps processing audio with no editor attached.

Seen on Windows with a VST3 (FetCB) on the master fader: once in this state, the editor would not open again until the session was reloaded.

## Fix

The host only hands over an instance when it no longer tracks the one in the slot, so an instance waiting for a slot now always replaces whatever the slot holds. This applies to both inserts and instruments (`SlotCtx::waiting`).

Also added: `debug` logs on the UI thread when an instance is created and when one is released, to make problems like this easy to trace from `soundcraft.log`.

## Tests

- New regression test: `a_new_instance_replaces_a_matching_one_in_its_slot`. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-mix -p soundcraft-playback`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` all pass on these crates.

title: Signal Generator fills the selection with a new clip
author: grovebit
body:
Fixes #220: Render in the Signal Generator did nothing on a time selection over an empty part of a track, because AudioSuite only processed the clips under the selection.

- A generator (today only the Signal Generator) renders a new clip over exactly the selection on each selected audio track, over whatever is there, as in Pro Tools. Before, it replaced whole clips under the selection and left the gaps empty.
- Effects and explicit `clips` work as before. With no audio track in the selection, it says so.
- The AudioSuite window's hint says what Render does for a generator.

title: Say at the Record button why Record did nothing
author: grovebit

Fixes #316: in a new session, clicking Record did nothing visible. The reason only went to the end of the dim status line, and it pointed at a track header that didn't exist yet.

- Record with nothing to record on shows a note for 4 seconds under the toolbar's Record button and the Transport window's, as well as in the status line.

title: Add tracks from the Tracks list and the empty space below the tracks
author: grovebit
body:
Part of #307: adding a track took the Track menu or Shift+Cmd+N (Shift+Ctrl+N on Windows and Linux). Nothing on screen offered it, not even in an empty session.

title: Refuse corrupt audio files instead of crashing
author: grovebit
body:
A corrupt audio file of a few dozen bytes could end the app on import: symphonia allocates whatever size a file claims before reading it, and a failed allocation aborts the process, which no `catch_unwind` can stop (on main, 10 of 1,343 mutated files did, and 8 more took over 2 GB).

- CAF and MP4 files are walked the way symphonia reads them before it does, and one whose cookie, packet table, sample table, atom or sample claims more than the file holds is refused as malformed. Files cut short, like a recording whose `mdat` ends early, still open.
- A packet may hold at most 2^20 frames, and so may an ALAC frame (a 59 KB ALAC file took 25 GB).
- FLAC picture and comment lengths and WAV INFO entries are checked against their block or file first, and ID3v2 tags ahead of the audio are skipped by their size instead of read.

Tested: 687 tests pass, 9 of them new (crafted CAF, MP4, ALAC, LPCM, FLAC, ID3 and WAV files); fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass; the 1,343 mutated files through `soundcraft-cli info` and `convert` give no crash or hang and use at most 24 MB. Six VST3 tests are skipped because they abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Keep corrupt sessions and imports from hanging, crashing or filling memory
author: grovebit
body:
Session, MIDI, clip group and audio files could hang the app, crash it or fill its memory: a sample rate of 0 hung Strip Silence, a path to /dev/zero filled 18 GB, a million-character track name crashed every frame, and clips near i64::MAX made a dozen commands overflow.

- Loading a session now repairs its sample rate and tempo map, cuts names to 256 characters and keeps positions within the ±2^40 samples commands already use.
- Devices and pipes are refused where a file is expected, audio is size-checked at the session rate before it is converted, and each audio file is decoded once however many sources name it.
- MIDI files longer than a day or with more than 10,000 meter changes are refused, same-named tracks and files are numbered in linear time, and Extract Chords skips bars where nothing sounds.

Tested: 695 tests pass, 17 of them new; fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass; setting 25 position fields to extremes under 65 commands gave 68 overflow panics and 6 hangs in a debug build of main and none here, and a session naming one WAV 2,000 times opens in 0.1 s and 110 MB instead of 16 s and 22 GB. Six VST3 tests are skipped because they abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Stop Strip Silence deleting clips late in long selections
author: grovebit
body:
Strip Silence rendered the whole selection at once, and a render stops at 2^29 samples over all channels (93 minutes of stereo at 48 kHz), so every clip past that read as silence and was deleted.

- It renders 2^24-sample windows (at most 64 MB each), only where unmuted audio clips play, into a streaming silence detector.
- More than a day of clips is refused instead of scanned for minutes.
- Mix renders skip muted clips and clips outside their range before looking up clip effects, so a track of 5,000 clips strips as fast as before.

Tested: 681 tests pass, 3 of them new; fmt, clippy, assets, layers and wasm pass; a 105-minute stereo selection keeps its clip at 100 minutes, and results match main on the demo sessions and on 10 minutes of tone bursts that cross window edges. Six VST3 tests are skipped because they abort when third-party VST3s are installed.

title: Fix clip fade editing and add live waveform previews
author: reoniazx
body:
Fade drags can currently draw outside their clip, use a different curve while dragging, and leave the waveform unchanged until release. This PR keeps the fade preview inside the clip and makes its curve and waveform update together during the drag, matching the committed result.

## Changes

- Use the same thin curve renderer for previews and stored fades, with bounded sampling based on physical pixel size to avoid visible corners on steep curves.
- Make existing fades draggable from their upper endpoints and add persistent midpoint controls for continuous curvature adjustment. Length drags retain the chosen shape and curvature.
- Preview waveform amplitude during both fade-length and curvature drags, retaining clip gain, gain envelopes, waveform zoom and display modes. Reuse decoded audio and cached peaks, and commit once on release for a single undo step.
- Extend `edit.fades_create` with targeted `{clip, side, length, shape?, curvature?}` parameters so a full-clip fade updates only the intended side. Existing range-based fades/crossfades retain their behavior.
- Save optional fade `curvature` in sessions, defaulting to zero for older files so their envelopes remain unchanged. Bound curvature values and harden gain-envelope arithmetic for extreme sample positions.

## Validation

- `cargo xtask ci` passes on this branch based on the latest upstream `main`: formatting, workspace Clippy, workspace tests, asset attribution, architecture layers and WASM check.
- Regression coverage includes clip bounds, full-clip/one-sample fades, adjacent clip boundaries, repeat midpoint grabs after extreme bends, clip removal/shrink during a drag, and one-step undo/redo.
- Waveform previews are checked in mono/stereo with Peak, Power, Rectified and Outlines modes, waveform zoom and clip gain envelopes. Geometry must change while the button is held and match after release; neighboring clips and cached media remain unchanged.
- Model/mixer tests verify bounded monotonic envelopes, aud…

title: Arabic (العربية) UI translation: language switching + font fallback
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
A full i18n.rs catalog (1,368 entries) for the whole interface — every menu label (including the docking panel titles at their display points), dialog, toolbar control and status message — written from the plain meaning of the English with the audio-engineering vocabulary Arabic DAW users know (تتبّع، توجيه، تخزين مؤقت، وحدة التأثيرات، متلاشية، التفريغ…), with count-neutral wording where English pluralizes.

- **Switch** — the اللغة submenu in the SoundCraft menu, so the language changes without a trip to a config file.
- **Fonts** — the Arabic chain (Noto Sans Arabic, Segoe UI, Tahoma, Geeza Pro…) appended to the Proportional families so the UI paints Arabic out of the box.

No layout mirroring in this PR: egui 0.36 has no global direction switch and no bidi reordering, so the shell still lays out left-to-right and the words of an Arabic label come out in reverse order until a bidi pass (the approach discussed in vectorcraft#1202) lands. I kept this PR to the catalog, the language switch and the fonts rather than pretend at mirroring an API that doesn't exist.

title: Honor session and track recording disk allocation
author: ProdByBuddha
body:

title: Add Clip > New MIDI Clip
author: Limestudio90
body:
## What

Adds **Clip > New MIDI Clip**.

A new MIDI or instrument track has no clip, and the MIDI Editor, the MIDI Keyboard window and step entry all need one. The `midi.new_clip` command already existed but could only be reached by command id, so there was no way to get a clip from the UI on an empty track.

The menu entry runs `midi.new_clip` on the selected track: the clip covers the edit selection, or one bar when nothing is selected.

## How

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/midi.rs`: `midi.new_clip` gets the menu path `Clip`.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`: the entry is added in `menus::tree()`, like `Window > Reset Panel Layout`, instead of to `catalog/menus.txt`. That file lists only the reference app's menu leaves and drives the parity numbers, so a SoundCraft-only entry does not belong there. The menu resolves to the command by label and menu path.

## Tests

- New test in `menus.rs`: the Clip menu lists the entry, it resolves to `midi.new_clip`, and invoking it on an instrument track creates one clip.
- `cargo fmt`, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` on `soundcraft-engine` and `soundcraft-ui-egui`, all `soundcraft-ui-egui` tests, `soundcraft-engine` lib tests, `xtask layers` and `xtask assets` pass.
- Known unrelated failures on Windows: `soundcraft-engine` `saved_audio_is_trusted_only_in_the_folder_it_was_saved_in`, and `clippy -D warnings` on the whole workspace stops at `soundcraft-video` (`collapsible_match` in `isobmff/codec.rs`) on current `main`.

title: fix(mix): mix.insert_params rejects unknown parameter names
author: mroxso
body:
## What

`mix.insert_params` silently dropped keys that don't match a plugin parameter, so a typo like `gain_db` instead of `gain` returned `{"ok": true, "set": 0}` — indistinguishable from a successful no-op (#266).

## How

- The command now validates every key against the plugin's parameter list **before** applying anything: unknown ids fail with `` `gain` has no parameter(s): gain_db ``, and known keys with non-numeric/non-finite values fail with a list too. A mixed batch changes nothing when it fails (validate-then-apply), so callers never see a partial silent write.
- This matches how `mix.insert` already rejects unknown params.
- Preset recall in the plugin menu (the one in-repo caller) now filters saved preset files down to the parameters the plugin currently exposes, so old presets across plugin versions still recall instead of erroring.
- `{params: {}, preset: name}` (the rename path used by Save) still succeeds.
- Updated the command's params doc shown by `engine.commands`/`list_commands`.

## Tests

- New unit test `insert_params_rejects_unknown_and_non_numeric_keys` covering the typo case from the issue, mixed batches, non-numeric/null values, clamping, and the preset-rename path.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes (fmt, clippy, tests, assets, layers). The wasm step fails locally only because the Homebrew toolchain here has no `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target installed; the change uses portable std/serde_json only.

Fixes #266

title: Isolate document recovery directories and validate reused audio
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Same-named documents and reused source IDs must not share recovery media. This change atomically reserves a directory for each document lifetime, shares it with unsaved recording and the existing background autosave writer, and verifies available audio before reusing a recovery WAV. Changed candidates receive fresh filenames.

Directory changes are queued on the existing writer, so rebinding does not join a thread on the UI path. Current main's worker scheduling, flush behavior, recovery format, locking and successful-save cleanup are preserved. New/Open/Close/Revert start a new logical lifetime; edits, undo/redo, Save As and Save Copy retain it. Physical reservations can renew after cleanup.

Validation: `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passed all six gates on isolated Linux: fmt, strict Clippy, tests, assets, layers and WASM. The run recorded 1,067 passes, zero failures, one existing ignore and zero filters, including all 16 focused recovery/lifetime cases. Those cover queued directory switches, reused IDs, changed WAV bytes, read-root admission, cleanup, and partial-take recovery.

Encoding and verification run in the background but still have CPU, temporary-memory and disk-I/O costs. This adds no retention policy or unavailable-media repair; temporary fallback paths do not gain automatic discovery outside the configured root.

title: Restore missing audio with validated manual relinking
author: ProdByBuddha

Add **Session Audio Health > Relink Audio** and the `media.relink` / `source.relink` commands to restore a selected source while preserving IDs, clip timing, alternate takes and stored BWF time-reference metadata, with undo/redo.

Channel/frame/rate checks and an optional versioned SHA-256 identity reject wrong audio. Legacy sources require explicit confirmation, which cannot override a known identity mismatch. The dialog retains errors for retry, refreshes Audio Health after relink/undo/redo, and discards consent after successful document replacement.

Rebased on current main. Preserve its file-access guard and shared audio decoding while validating each source independently. Save/bundle aliases and the background autosaver retain identities of actual encoded PCM; imported session audio is verified before rate conversion and reidentified afterward. Existing recovery-copy cleanup remains in place. Identities follow the current encoded audio, including existing WAV clamping.

Validation on Rust 1.95.0:

- Full unchanged `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passed in isolated Linux: formatting, strict workspace/all-target Clippy, tests, asset attribution, layers and WASM. 1,073 standard tests passed; zero failed, one existing ignored, zero filtered. All 17 engine and four UI relinking cases passed.
- Both current-source synthetic offscreen dialogs rendered at 3200×2000 and passed visual review. This verifies rendered UI; native macOS picker/audio-device acceptance remains separate.

Scope is native, user-selected audio relinking. Exact PCM comparison can conservatively reject a candidate after decoder or sample-rate conversion changes. Large-file hashing/save performance remains unmeasured.

title: Preserve Float32 headroom in audio files and saved sources

body:
Float32 output currently clips a finite sample such as `1.25` to `1.0`. Preserve finite sample bits in WAV/RF64 and AIFF-C files, including headroom, signed zero and subnormals, and write zero for NaN and infinity. Apply the same nonfinite policy on the take writer thread.

Integer quantization, clipping and TPDF dither retain their existing behavior. Tests cover actual PCM payloads and byte order, distinct multichannel samples, streamed output, integer/dither policy, take serialization, and generated-source folder saves, Save Copy and session bundles. The real-time callback and ring-buffer behavior are unchanged.

Full unchanged `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passed on Rust 1.95.0 in isolated Linux: formatting, strict workspace/all-target Clippy, tests, asset attribution, layers and WASM. 1,058 standard tests passed, zero failed, one existing ignored and zero filtered; all 10 focused cases passed. Recording coverage uses synthetic writer inputs. No UI pixels changed.

title: Prevent track-name collisions after truncation
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Track rename checks the requested name for collisions before truncating it to 64 Unicode scalars. A long request can therefore store another track's name and return a value different from storage. Validate the trimmed, truncated name before mutation and return that exact name.

When neither the stored track name nor its owned folder bus needs changing, the rename preserves the document revision, dirty state and Undo history. Successful requests retain current command-journal behavior. Preserve current main's routing-folder bus naming and repair, unique bus names, stable member routes, and undo/redo. Tests cover ASCII and CJK collisions, exact returned names, no-op state, and folder behavior.

Rebased on current main. No UI code changes.

title: Hosted plugins: stop pushing their early 0 readings back (Rhapsody played silence)
author: Limestudio90
body:
## What

Hosted plugins that report 0 for their parameters until they load their own preset came up silenced: volume and pan at minimum, every control at 0. Seen with Rhapsody (a HISE player, 6 stereo outputs, 2112 parameters), which restores its last library on its own. Notes arrived and the instrument played nothing. Whether it happened depended on whether the library finished loading before or after the first audio block, so it looked random.

The zeros reached the plugin from two places:

1. **`vst3-host`: `Vst3Plugin::prepare` re-sent every cached parameter value.** The cache is first filled by reading the plugin right after it is created, so those early readings (0) went back to the plugin on the first block. This was the main cause.
   Values the host set (`set_param`) are now tracked and only those are re-sent on activation. Readings taken from the plugin stay with the plugin.
2. **`mix.instrument` / `mix.insert` filled a hosted plugin's parameter map with the defaults it reports**, and the mix engine pushed that map on the first block. Sessions saved that way keep the zeros (Rhapsody: 2112 entries).
   - A hosted plugin (CLAP, VST3, Audio Unit, JSFX) now starts with an empty parameter map (`fill_default_params`). Built-in plugins still get their defaults.
   - On the first parameter pass of a hosted plugin, `apply_values` skips a stored value equal to the default the plugin reports. Sessions saved by older versions are fixed this way. Other stored values still apply after the restored state (`stored_state_comes_first_then_session_params` is unchanged), and every later change is pushed, including a return to the default.

Plugin states captured *while* the plugin was zeroed hold the zeros themselves. For those, removing and re-adding the plugin is still needed.

## Testing

- New: `vst3-host` `only_values_the_host_set_are_re_sent`; `mix` `a_hosted_plugin_keeps_its_own_values_where_the_session_holds_its_defaults` (fails without the change); `engine` `hosted_p…

title: fix(mix): apply MIDI clip fades on instrument tracks (#274)
author: salignatmoandal
body:
## Summary
- `edit.fades_create` stores `fade_in` / `fade_out` / clip gain on MIDI clips, but the mix engine only applied `Clip::gain_at` inside `render_clip` (audio). Instrument tracks schedule notes into one synth and never faded the output — success + stored state + bit-identical bounce (#274).

- [ ] Bounce an instrument clip before/after `edit.fades_create` and confirm LUFS/peak change

Fixes #274

title: Add atomic batch track naming with preview and one Undo

title: Select an independent Bounce Mix delivery sample rate
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Bounce Mix can select a delivery sample rate independently of the session. The command accepts integer Hz from 8,000 through 768,000, and the dialog offers presets and Custom with the session rate selected initially. The default dialog choice retains the existing streaming bounce path.

The mixer and plugins remain at the session rate. Explicit changed-rate delivery converts once after source selection and optional stereo fold, before normalization, output-rate measurements and encoding. Bounded work slices retain progress and cancellation; allocation, plugin and disk work have no hard timing guarantee. Results report actual rate, frame count and duration.

Explicit delivery plans reject invalid rates, zero-frame conversions, unsupported declared widths and oversized buffers before rendering or replacing a destination. Equal-rate delivery retains the encoded bytes and measurements. Current file-root guards, Browse, format inference and the progressive bounce lifecycle are preserved.

Rebased on current main. The feature documentation contains project behavior, limits and tests only. Stems, quality options, noise shaping and pull-up/down remain separate.

Validation: unchanged full Linux CI passed all six gates (fmt, strict workspace/all-targets Clippy, tests, assets, layers and WASM): 1,067 passed, 0 failed, 1 existing ignored, 0 filtered.
