- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

title: fix(ui): add Fedora font paths so DejaVu and Liberation load on Fedora (#45)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #45 (part 2: the Fedora font paths).

**Cause.** `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs`'s `REGULAR` / `BOLD` tables list the Debian/Ubuntu (`/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu`, `/usr/share/fonts/TTF`, `/usr/share/fonts/dejavu`) and Arch (`/usr/local/share/fonts/dejavu`) layouts for DejaVu, and one `truetype/liberation` path for Liberation. None of these match Fedora's `dejavu-sans-fonts` and `liberation-sans-fonts` package layout:

- `/usr/share/fonts/dejavu-sans-fonts/DejaVuSans.ttf` (and `-Bold`)
- `/usr/share/fonts/liberation-sans-fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf`

On Fedora, `load_from_fontconfig` (called first in `load`) may also return `None` — e.g. when only Liberation Sans is installed, or when the `sans-serif` fontconfig alias doesn't point at DejaVu — so the direct-path fallback runs and finds nothing. The app falls back to egui's built-in fonts, which don't include the menu glyphs (`→ ▸ ▾ ♯ ✕`), so they render as empty boxes.

**Fix.** Add the two Fedora paths to the `REGULAR` and `BOLD` candidates, in the same order as the existing Debian and Arch paths. `load` still tries `load_from_fontconfig` first; the direct paths are the fallback when fontconfig doesn't surface a usable face.

**Build.** `cargo test -p soundcraft-ui-egui` → 105 passed, 0 failed. No new tests: the table is data, and exercising it on Fedora would require running a real `fc-match` against the actual system fonts.

title: fix(mcp): reject oversized batches before execution
author: euisuh
body:
MCP batches currently execute only the first 1,000 entries and can report success after silently omitting the remainder. Reject oversized batches before dispatching any command, for both keep_going values, and advertise the same limit in the tool schema and docs. Valid batches keep their existing order and error handling.

The regression initially created a track from a 1,001-entry batch. With the fix, the session, journal and undo history remain unchanged and the tool reports an error. Boundary coverage also checks empty and exactly 1,000-entry batches.

### Validation

- `cargo xtask ci`: PASS, including formatting, workspace all-target Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, assets, layers and WASM.
- Workspace: 1,064 tests passed; one existing speed benchmark ignored.
- Targeted automation suite: all 18 tests pass; targeted all-target typecheck and Clippy pass.
- Independent parent source/test review completed. No dependencies, persistence schema or authentication changes.

Closes #460

title: WAV: an empty data chunk followed by metadata has no frames (#466)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #466

## Cause

`wav::parse` (`crates/audio-io/src/wav.rs`) reads a non-RF64 data chunk whose size is 0 as "everything that follows". That is meant for a recording that was never finalised (a streaming writer leaves the sizes at 0 until it finishes). But a finished, valid, empty WAV also has a data size of 0, and often a `LIST` or `bext` chunk after it: those bytes were then decoded as samples and the file reported frames it does not have.

## Fix

A zero data size is now read as empty when the file looks finished: the RIFF size is the file's size and everything after the data chunk is whole RIFF chunks (`only_chunks_follow`: printable-ASCII ids, sizes that fit, pad bytes, the last chunk's pad may be missing). Then the chunks after it are scanned normally, so `bext` is still read. In every other case the lenient behaviour is unchanged: an unfinalised recording (RIFF size 0, or audio that is not a run of chunks) still gives the audio that was written. Files with a non-zero data size are not touched.

## Verified

New `crates/audio-io/tests/wav_empty_data.rs`:

- `an_empty_data_chunk_followed_by_metadata_has_no_frames`: LIST + bext after an empty data chunk, metadata before it, and a last odd-sized chunk without its pad byte all give 0 frames through `probe` and `decode`. **Fails on `main`** (`probe` reports frames made of the metadata) and passes here.
- `a_recording_that_was_never_finalised_still_gives_its_audio`: RIFF and data size both 0 followed by 200 stereo frames still decode to 200 frames; so does a file whose RIFF size is right but that has raw audio (not chunks) after the empty data chunk. Passes on `main` and here (control).
- `a_data_chunk_with_audio_is_unchanged`: 100 frames, followed by metadata, still 100 (control).

The rest of the `soundcraft-audio-io` suite (including `malformed.rs`' truncation and corruption tests) passes. `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed

- Recovery of unfinished recordings is still the same lenient read; I did not a…

title: Sampler: a ping-pong loop keeps its phase for steps wider than the loop (#463)
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #463

## Cause

`advance` in `crates/dsp/src/plugins/sampler.rs` reflected a ping-pong voice at the loop's end (or start) once and then clamped it to the loop (`.max(ls)` / `.min(le)`). A step wider than the loop (a narrow loop with high transposition or sample-rate conversion) crosses the loop more than once in one output frame; the clamp threw away the rest of the travel, so the loop phase and the effective pitch were wrong.

## Fix

The distance travelled past the edge it was heading for is folded into the loop: an even number of crossings keeps the direction, an odd number turns it round, and the position is `edge ± the remainder`. Steps narrower than the loop move exactly as before (a single reflection gives the same position and direction as the old code). Non-finite positions are left to the existing check that stops the voice, and a loop whose width is not positive keeps going through the existing path.

## Verified

Tests in `plugins::sampler::tests`:

- `a_ping_pong_step_wider_than_the_loop_keeps_the_phase`: a voice in a 10-frame loop, moving forwards and backwards, with steps 0.37, 3, 9.99, 10, 10.5, 23.7, 25, 31.3 and 99.9, for 40 steps each, compared at every step with an independent triangle-wave reference (position within 1e-6, direction too, except exactly on an end where it is the direction it is heading next). **Fails on `main`** and passes here.
- `a_ping_pong_step_below_the_loop_width_moves_as_before`: reflections off the end and the start with step 5 in the same loop. Passes on `main` and here (control).
- The existing `ping_pong_loop_reverses_direction` still passes.

`cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed

- The plain forward loop mode already folds with `%` and is untouched.
- Whether the voice's direction at an exact endpoint should be "arriving" or "leaving" is as it was: it turns at the edge.

## AI disclosure

This PR was prepared by an AI coding agent (Claude Code) on behalf of @Silvertree2010 and tested as described above.

title: Reject out-of-range signed Exp-Golomb codes instead of wrapping (#473)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #473.

`BitReader::read_se` mapped an odd `ue(v)` code `k` to `(k + 1) / 2` and cast it to `i32` without a range check. `read_ue` can return up to `u32::MAX`, and that code maps to `+2^31`, which does not fit in `i32`. The cast wrapped it to `i32::MIN`, so a malformed stream was accepted with the wrong sign.

The positive branch now uses `i32::try_from` and returns `BitError::InvalidExpGolomb`, the same error `read_ue` already returns when its own value does not fit in `u32`. The negative branch cannot overflow (its largest magnitude is `2^31 - 1`), so it is unchanged. The `InvalidExpGolomb` doc comment now also mentions out-of-range values.

Test: `read_se_rejects_unrepresentable_positive` writes the codes `u32::MAX`, `u32::MAX - 1` and `u32::MAX - 2` and reads them with `read_se`. The first now returns `InvalidExpGolomb` (without the fix it returns `Ok(i32::MIN)`). The other two still decode to the representable extremes, `-i32::MAX` and `i32::MAX`.

title: Reject invalid numeric prereleases and restore Cargo.toml when version update fails (#471)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #471.

`cargo xtask version set` accepted versions that Cargo rejects, and once it had rewritten the root `Cargo.toml` a failed `cargo update` left the broken manifest in place.

How each point of the issue is handled:

- **Leading-zero numeric prerelease ids** (`1.0.0-01`, `1.0.0-rc.01`): `validate()` now rejects a purely numeric prerelease identifier with a leading zero, as the semver crate Cargo uses does. Alphanumeric ids such as `01a` are still allowed, as SemVer allows.
- **Numeric bounds**: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` must fit in `u64` (`99999999999999999999.0.0` is now rejected). Numeric prerelease ids are not limited in length, because Cargo accepts them at any length, so `1.0.0-99999999999999999999` stays valid.
- **Manifest left changed on failure**: the write-then-update step is now a small `set()` helper. If `cargo update` fails (offline and then online), it writes the old manifest back with the same atomic write it used for the new one. The error message says whether the restore worked.

Tests:
- `rejects_what_cargo_rejects`: the invalid cases from the issue fail in `validate()` and `replace()`. Edge cases that Cargo accepts still pass.
- `a_failed_update_restores_the_manifest`: runs `set()` on a temporary manifest with a failing update step and checks that the file is byte-for-byte the original. A succeeding update step writes the new version.

Only `xtask/src/version.rs` changes.

title: Read MP4 ctts version 0 composition offsets as unsigned (#470)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #470.

`parse_stbl` threw away the `ctts` version and cast every composition offset through `i32`. In ISO BMFF, version 0 offsets are unsigned and only version 1 offsets are signed, so a version 0 offset above `i32::MAX` became negative and broke presentation timing.

The parser now keeps the `ctts` version:

- version 0: offsets are read as unsigned
- version 1: offsets are read as signed, as before
- QuickTime files (`is_quicktime`): offsets stay signed in every version, because the QuickTime spec defines `ctts` offsets as signed. Apple MOVs with negative version 0 offsets read the same as before.

This works the same way as the fragmented `trun` path in the same file, which already reads `v == 0` offsets as unsigned and `v == 1` as signed. Our own muxer writes `ctts` version 1 whenever an offset is negative, so files it writes still round-trip.

Test: `ctts_version0_offsets_are_unsigned` takes the handmade file, which has version 1 `ctts` with `-5` offsets, and changes it to version 0. It checks that the offsets now read as `0xFFFFFFFB`. Then it changes the major brand to `qt  ` and checks that they read as `-5` again. The existing `handmade_sample_table` test still covers negative version 1 offsets. The new test fails on main, where the version 0 file reads `-5`.

title: Reject invalid NAL length-field width in length_prefixed_nals (#469)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #469.

`length_prefixed_nals` with `length_size == 0` never advances the cursor and pushes empty slices forever, so a nonempty input loops while memory grows. Widths above 4 are also not valid AVCC/HVCC prefix sizes.

Changes (`crates/video/src/bitstream.rs`):
- Reject any `length_size` outside `1..=4` at entry with a new `BitError::InvalidLengthSize` ("invalid NAL length-field size").
- Check the payload bound as `len > data.len() - i` instead of `i + len > data.len()`, so a 4-byte length near `u32::MAX` cannot overflow on 32-bit targets (the issue's second suggestion, checked cursor arithmetic).
- Doc comment now says 1 to 4 bytes.

The only in-tree caller (H.264 decoder) passes the avcC `lengthSizeMinusOne + 1`, which is always 1 to 4, so its behaviour is unchanged.

Test: `length_prefixed_rejects_bad_width` checks that widths 0 and 5 return `InvalidLengthSize` and a valid 1-byte prefix still splits. Without the fix, the width-0 case never returns. The existing 2- and 4-byte tests are kept.

title: Count the partial quartet in the base64 decoded-size cap (#468)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #468.

`b64::decode` checked its `MAX_DECODED_BYTES` cap with `body.len() / 4 * 3`, which leaves out the 1 or 2 bytes from a final partial quartet. A valid encoding of `MAX_DECODED_BYTES + 1` or `+ 2` bytes got through. The check also ran only after every non-whitespace symbol had been copied into a `Vec`, however long the input was.

Changes, both in `crates/model/src/b64.rs`:

- Before allocating anything, `decode` counts the non-whitespace symbols and returns `None` if there are more than any in-cap encoding can have (`MAX_DECODED_BYTES.div_ceil(3) * 4`).
- The cap check now uses the exact decoded length, partial quartet included (`body.len() / 4 * 3 + body.len() % 4 * 3 / 4`). The output `Vec` is allocated with that same length.

Valid input under the cap decodes exactly as before. The only caller that reports the error (`mix.insert_state`) already says "not valid base64 (or is too large)", so nothing else changes.

Test: `size_cap_counts_the_partial_quartet` encodes cap-1, cap, cap+1 and cap+2 bytes and decodes each one padded, unpadded and with whitespace inside. On `main` the cap+1 cases are accepted, so the test fails there.

title: Return TooLarge when the WAV header size overflows u64 (#467)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #467.

`wav::header` computed the data length with `checked_mul`, but then added the container overhead and the odd-byte pad with plain `+`. A frame count just under `u64::MAX / block_align` passed the multiplication and overflowed on the addition: debug builds panicked, release builds produced a wrapped size.

The total is now built with `checked_add` and returns `AudioError::TooLarge` on overflow, the same error the multiplication above already returns. `wav_float_header` and `FileEncoder::check_room` / `write` for WAV both go through `wav::header`, so all of these paths now return the error instead.

Test: `float_wav_header_rejects_a_frame_count_whose_total_size_overflows` calls `wav_float_header(1, 48_000, u64::MAX / 4)`. Without the fix it panics on the overflow. With the fix it returns `TooLarge`.

title: Validate the full WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE fmt chunk (#465)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #465.

`parse_fmt` in `crates/audio-io/src/wav.rs` read only the first two bytes of the extensible subtype GUID and took them as the format tag. So a truncated extension, or a foreign subtype whose GUID starts with `01 00` / `03 00`, was decoded as native PCM/float.

The extensible branch now checks the points the issue lists:

- **Extension length:** the chunk must hold the whole 40-byte extensible layout (cbSize, valid bits, channel mask, 16-byte GUID). A shorter one is `Malformed`.
- **cbSize:** below 22 is `Malformed`.
- **Valid bits:** more valid bits than the container's `wBitsPerSample` is `Malformed`. A value of 0 still means "same as the container", as before.
- **Full GUID:** the subtype tag is used only when GUID bytes 2..16 match the `KSDATAFORMAT_SUBTYPE_*` tail (`GUID_TAIL`, the same constant the writer emits). Any other GUID keeps the extensible tag, so the file takes the existing `WavParse::Foreign` path to symphonia, like other codecs we don't decode natively. Malformed extensions and unsupported foreign subtypes are told apart, as the issue asks.

Files written by our own encoder (cbSize 22, valid bits = bits, standard GUID) parse as before.

### Tests

`extensible_fmt_is_checked_in_full` in `crates/audio-io/tests/malformed.rs` builds extensible WAVs through the public `probe`/`decode` API:

- standard PCM GUID → still `Int16`;
- GUID cut after the format code → `Malformed` (probe and decode);
- cbSize 0 → `Malformed`;
- 24 valid bits in a 16-bit container → `Malformed`;
- PCM prefix with a changed GUID tail → no longer read as native `Int16`.

Each of the last four cases is accepted as native PCM on current main, so the test fails without the fix.

title: Keep audio-io stream test limits as u64 so it compiles on 32-bit targets (#462)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #462.

The format-limit test in `crates/audio-io/tests/stream.rs` typed its format limits as `usize` (`1usize << 30`), so the FLAC limit `1 << 36` overflowed and the test failed to compile on 32-bit targets.

- The limits are now `u64`, and `check_room` takes them directly.
- The `write` call converts the limit with `usize::try_from`. It is skipped when the limit does not fit in `usize`. On 64-bit targets the test runs exactly as before.

This change is test-only. No library code changes.

title: Reject MOV PCM frame widths that overflow u32 (#461)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #461.

`PcmConfig::bytes_per_frame` multiplied bytes per sample by the channel count in plain `u32`. A huge channel count (a public writer config, or a QuickTime v2 sound description, where channels is a full `u32`) panicked in debug builds and wrapped in release, so the writer could keep a wrong frame width, including zero, and later divide sample data by it.

- `PcmConfig::checked_bytes_per_frame` returns `None` when the width does not fit in `u32`.
- `bytes_per_frame` now saturates at `u32::MAX` instead of panicking or wrapping. The demuxer uses it to size PCM chunks, so a file with a bogus channel count gets oversized chunks that fail to read instead of a panic or a wrapped size.
- `Mp4Writer`'s `validate_track` uses the checked width and returns `Error::Mux` when it overflows, like its other PCM checks. The existing `bits == 0 || channels == 0` check already rules out a zero width.

Tests: `pcm_frame_width_overflow` (codec) and `pcm_frame_width_overflow_is_rejected` (writer: `add_track` with `channels: u32::MAX` returns an error; without the fix it panics on the multiplication).

title: Do not retry remote-control commands that may already have run (#458)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #458.

`Remote::call` retried any request once after a "closed" / "Broken pipe" / "reset" error, even when the request line had already been written and the app may have executed it. A lost reply to `engine.execute` (for example `track.new`) could then apply the edit twice.

**Change** (`crates/automation/src/lib.rs` only):
- `roundtrip` now reports, together with the error, whether the request line was already written to the socket. Connect and write failures count as "not sent"; read, EOF, parse and app errors count as "sent".
- `call` still retries once on a fresh connection when the request was not sent, or when the method only reads state (`session.inspect`, `document.inspect`, `engine.commands`, `engine.parity`, `ui.inspect`, `ui.menu.list`; these are the read-only handlers in `ui-egui/src/control.rs`).
- In every other case it does not resend. It returns the original error plus a note that the command may or may not have been executed, so the caller can check the session before trying again.

**Tests:** a fake local TCP app reads one request and drops the connection without a reply, then answers ok on the next connection.
- `remote_does_not_repeat_a_mutation_after_a_lost_reply`: `engine.execute` returns the "may or may not have been executed" error, and the fake app sees the request only once. Without the fix the request is resent and the call succeeds, so the test fails.
- `remote_retries_a_read_after_a_lost_reply`: `session.inspect` is still retried and succeeds, with two requests seen.

No server-side deduplication was added. Stable operation IDs would need a protocol change in the app, which is a maintainer decision.

title: Keep controller-only tracks when importing MIDI (#454)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #454.

`import_midi_bytes` skipped every SMF track without notes, so a track holding only controller events (CC, pitch bend, program, aftertouch) was dropped on import, even though MIDI export now writes controllers.

Changes in `crates/engine/src/io.rs`:

- A track is skipped only when it has neither notes nor controller events. This matches `read_smf`, which drops the format-1 conductor track only when it has no notes and no controllers.
- The drum check (`all notes on channel 9`) was true for a track with no notes, so a controller-only track would have got a drum synth. It now needs at least one note, and a controller-only track gets the normal `subtractive_synth`.
- The imported clip now runs one tick past the last controller event. Playback only sends events that start before the clip end (`at < clip.end()` in the mixer), so a clip ending exactly on its last controller never played it. Before, a track with notes had the same problem when its last controller came after its last note end.

Test: `a_controller_only_midi_track_is_imported_with_its_events` writes an SMF with one track holding three CC7 events at ticks 0, 480 and 960. It imports the file and checks that one track is created with `subtractive_synth`, that the clip extends past the last event, and that the clip keeps the events with their kinds, values and ticks. Without the fix, the import returns no tracks and the test fails.

title: Scale fades, sync point and gain envelope when importing a clip group at another sample rate (#453)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #453.

`clip_group_file::import` already converts clip starts, lengths and audio source offsets from the file's sample rate to the session rate, but left the other sample-based clip fields as they were. A group saved at 48 kHz and imported into a 96 kHz session kept the right overall duration, but its fades lasted half as long and its sync point and gain-envelope breakpoints sat at half their positions.

The fix runs the same `scale` closure over `fade_in.len`, `fade_out.len`, `sync_point` and every gain-envelope breakpoint offset before `c.sanitize()`, so the existing clamping still applies. These are all the sample-based fields on `Clip`. MIDI note positions are in ticks, and `stretch` is a ratio, so neither needs converting.

Test: `fades_sync_point_and_envelope_follow_the_sample_rate` writes a group file saved at half the session rate. The file has a clip with uneven fades, a sync point and two envelope breakpoints. After import, the test checks that every one of those positions has doubled, the same as the clip length. Without the fix, the fade, sync-point and envelope assertions fail.

title: Keep overlapping clips of a clip group when importing it (#452)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #452.

`clip_group_file::import` inserted each clip of a lane with `edit::place_clip`, which clears the clip's range first. A later clip in the same lane therefore cut away the overlapping part of an earlier one, so crossfade partners (or any internal overlap) did not round-trip.

Now each lane is prepared first, the ranges of all its clips are cleared on the destination track (removing only material that was there before the import), and then the whole lane is added in one go and the playlist sorted, the same as `place_clip` does for a single clip. Pre-existing material under the group is still replaced as before.

Fade lengths are not touched here (that is #453).

Test: `overlapping_clips_of_a_group_keep_their_overlap_on_import` imports a group with two MIDI clips at 0..1000 and 600..1600 and checks both keep their start and length. Without the fix the first clip is cut to 0..600.

title: Reset clip stretch after AudioSuite bakes it into the new source (#451)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #451.

`audiosuite.process` renders the clip with its stretch applied, then builds the replacement clip as a clone of the original. The clone kept `stretch`, so playback stretched the already-stretched audio a second time (and could leave a silent tail).

The replacement clip now gets `stretch = 1.0`, the same as the other commands that bake stretch into a new source (`clip.rs` render, `clip_more.rs` commit stretch, `edit_more.rs`, `io.rs`). Fades and gain handling are unchanged; the gain question from #88 is left as is.

Test: `processed_clip_does_not_keep_the_stretch_it_baked` runs Invert and Duplicate on clips at stretch 0.5 and 2.0 and checks that the new clip has stretch 1.0 and a length equal to the new source's frame count. It fails without the fix.

title: Heal keeps each clip's gain envelope and skips clips whose mute or stretch differ (#450)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #450.

`heal()` compared only the source, the offset and the static `gain_db` before it extended the left clip and dropped the right one. That had three effects:

- **Mute:** a muted right half took on the left half's mute state, and the reverse.
- **Gain envelope:** the right clip's envelope was lost. The left clip's points past the seam (separate leaves them in place) then played over the right half.
- **Stretch:** a right half with a different stretch ratio was played at the left ratio.

What this PR changes:

- Clips whose `muted` or `stretch` differ are no longer joined. A single clip can't hold two mute states or two ratios, so heal leaves that seam alone. This works the same way as the existing `gain_db` check.
- Gain envelopes are joined instead of refused. Refusing would stop Heal from undoing Separate on any clip that has an envelope, and that case works today. The new `join_gain_env` keeps the left clip's points before the seam, adds the right clip's points shifted by the left length, and adds a breakpoint on either side of the seam only where interpolation across it would change the gain. A plain separate-then-heal therefore adds no extra points to the left half, and the right half keeps the point that separate put at its start.
- `Clip::env_db_at` is a small public reader for the envelope value, built on the existing private `env_value`.

Tests in `crates/engine/src/edit.rs`:

- `heal_skips_clips_with_different_playback`: a right-only mute and a right-only stretch both leave two clips.
- `heal_keeps_each_side_gain_envelope`: four cases (left envelope only, right envelope only, both with a negative right point, and the exact split that separate produces). Each one compares `gain_at` on every sample of the healed clip with the two original halves. The right-only and left-only cases fail on `main`.

Not run locally (no Rust toolchain on this machine). I checked line widths against `max_width = 150` with `use_small_heuristics = "Max"`.

title: Keep unrelated overlapping clips untouched when deleting fades (#449)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #449.

`delete_fades` cleared fades only on clips touching the requested range, but then trimmed every overlapping neighbour pair in the playlist back to its midpoint. Deleting one crossfade therefore also shortened a separate crossfade further down the track.

The function now records the clips it cleared (a `HashSet<ClipId>`, like the other edit ops in `edit.rs`) and trims an overlapping pair only when at least one of its two clips is in that set. Overlaps outside the selection keep their boundaries, source offsets and fades. Inside the selection the behaviour is the same as before. `edit.fades_delete` is the only caller.

Test: `delete_fades_leaves_unrelated_overlaps_alone` builds two separate crossfades and deletes only the first. It checks that the first pair is trimmed to its midpoint with its fades cleared, and that the second pair keeps its start, length, source offset and fades. Without the fix the second pair gets trimmed to its midpoint and the test fails.

title: Load older sessions whose track height is the bare Fit string (#447)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #447.

Zoom Toggle (e26a5f5) changed `TrackHeight::Fit` from a unit variant to `Fit(u16)`. A session saved before that with a track height of `"Fit"` no longer deserializes, so `Session::from_json` fails and the session does not open.

`TrackHeight` now deserializes through a small adapter (`#[serde(from = ...)]`): an untagged enum that accepts the current form or the bare `"Fit"` string. The legacy `"Fit"` maps to `Medium`, which is 88 points, the same height the old `Fit` was drawn at, so these tracks look the same as before. Serialization is unchanged: `Fit(120)` still writes `{"Fit":120}`, and every other variant writes as before.

Tests:
- `track::tests::legacy_fit_string_loads_as_default_height`: `"Fit"` loads as `Medium`; `{"Fit":120}`, `"Large"` and `{"Custom":50}` still load; `Fit(120)` still serializes as `{"Fit":120}`.
- `session::tests::session_with_legacy_fit_height_loads`: a complete saved session with a track height of `"Fit"` loads through `Session::from_json` (the regression test the issue asks for).

Both fail on main (the `"Fit"` string is rejected) and pass with this change.

title: Fix bundle opening losing audio for sources that share one file (#446)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #446.

`open_session_bytes` took each source's bundle entry with `files.remove(&src.path)`, so when two source IDs point at the same file (which native sessions allow and save that way), only the first one got audio; every later one was reported missing and its clips went silent.

Now each path is decoded once and the resulting `Arc<SourceAudio>` is shared by every source that uses that path. A path that is absent or fails to decode is still reported once, as before.

Test: `sources_sharing_one_file_all_load_from_a_bundle` builds a bundle from the demo session with two source IDs pointing at one WAV, opens it, and checks that nothing is reported missing and every source has audio. Without the fix the second source is reported missing.

title: Keep MIDI note selection valid across clip, session and note-order changes (#443)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #443.

The MIDI Editor keeps the selected notes as indices into the edited clip's note list. Those indices went stale in three ways. Each one is handled here:

- **Clip switch.** When the editor moved to another clip, it updated the clip id and scroll, but kept the selection and any drag or rubber band in progress. Delete could then remove notes in the new clip. `MidiEditorState::switch_clip` now clears the selection, drag and band when the clip changes.
- **Session switch.** `session.new`, `session.open`, `session.close` and `session.revert` now reset the editor state. Otherwise a new session with the same clip id would keep the old selection.
- **Keyboard moves.** `midi.notes_move` re-sorts the notes, so after an arrow key moved a note past another one, the selection pointed at a different note. The command now also returns `indices`, the new positions of the moved notes, which works like `midi.note_edit` returning the edited note's new `index`. The arrow-key path sets the selection from it. The moved notes stay selected, so pressing the arrow again keeps nudging the same notes. Clearing the selection would have made every second press do nothing.

Drag-move already cleared the selection after `midi.notes_move`. That path is unchanged.

Tests:
- `midi_editor::tests::switching_clip_drops_selection_and_gestures`: a new clip clears the selection and gestures. The same clip keeps them.
- `tests::replacing_the_session_drops_the_midi_note_selection` (ui-egui `lib.rs`): `session.new` and `session.close` clear the MIDI selection.
- `cmd::midi::tests::notes_move_reports_where_the_moved_notes_went` (engine): a note moved past another one reports its new index.
- `pro_tools_keys::the_piano_roll_selection_follows_notes_the_arrows_move_past_others`: in the demo Keys clip, Shift+Up moves the lowest chord note an octave up, past the other two notes. The selection follows it for two presses. On main it kept pointing at index 0, which is now another note.

title: Reset clip effect EQ/compressor state on stop and seek (#442)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #442.

`MixEngine::reset` (called by playback on stop, locate and loop jumps) reset the strip inserts, the instrument and the delay-compensation lines, but not the cached Clip Effects chains in `Strip::clip_fx`. Replaying a clip after a stop or seek reused the EQ biquad history and the compressor's detector and lookahead delay from the old position, so the output differed from a fresh engine.

Change:
- `ClipFx::reset` resets the EQ and compressor when they exist, using the same `Plugin::reset` that the strip inserts already get.
- `MixEngine::reset` calls it for every cached clip chain on every strip.

Offline renders (`render_clips`) build a new `ClipFx` for each call, so they were not affected.

Test: `reset_clears_clip_effect_history` primes a DC clip through the clip compressor (5 ms lookahead), and separately through the clip EQ (high-pass on). It then resets, renders a later block, and compares that block with a fresh `MixEngine` rendering the same block. Both cases fail without the fix: the old lookahead samples and the settled high-pass state remain.

title: Create session backups exclusively and stop when backup numbers run out (#426)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #426.

`back_up` (crates/engine/src/io.rs) checked write access only on the `Backups` folder, picked the next number with `saturating_add(1)` and copied with `std::fs::copy`. When `Song backup 4294967295.scraft` already existed, the counter stuck at that number and the copy wrote through whatever was there, including a link to a file outside the automation write roots.

Each point of the issue's recommended remediation:

- **Validate the actual destination:** `check_write` now also runs on the backup file path itself, not only on the folder.
- **Reject counter exhaustion:** the next number uses `checked_add`; when it runs out, the backup is skipped with the same `log::warn!("no backup of …")` as the other failures in `back_up`, and the save goes on as before (a failed backup never failed a save).
- **Create exclusively without following existing entries:** the new `copy_new` helper opens the destination with `create_new(true)`, so an existing file or link (even a dangling one) makes the backup fail instead of being followed. A partly written copy is removed. This matches the `create_new` use a few lines below in the same file.

Ordinary saves are unchanged: numbering, the keep-the-newest-ten pruning and the warnings stay the same.

Tests (in `save_tests`):

- `backup_never_overwrites_an_existing_entry_when_numbers_run_out`: a `Song backup 4294967295.scraft` sentinel is left untouched by `back_up` (fails on main, which overwrote it), and `copy_new` refuses an existing destination.
- `backup_never_writes_through_a_link_to_an_outside_file` (Unix): the issue's scenario, a max-numbered backup link to an outside sentinel, plus a link at the next backup name; the outside file stays unchanged.
- The existing `saving_keeps_the_last_ten_versions_as_backups` still covers normal numbering and pruning.

title: fix(video): reject zero/invalid NAL length widths in length_prefixed_nals (#469)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #469.

## Summary

`length_prefixed_nals` in `crates/video/src/bitstream.rs` never validated its `length_size` argument. With a width of 0 and non-empty input, the cursor never advances — the prefix is 0 bytes and a zero length reads a 0-byte payload — so the loop spins indefinitely, appending empty NAL units until the process runs out of memory. Widths above 4 were also accepted even though an AVCC/HVCC record can only produce 1–4, and the cursor arithmetic was unchecked.

## Changes

- `crates/video/src/bitstream.rs` (+52/−8): reject any width outside `1..=4` up front with a new `BitError::InvalidLengthSize` variant. Width 3 stays valid: it is `lengthSizeMinusOne == 2`, produced by the crate's own AVCC/HVCC parsers.
- Same file: prefix and payload cursor arithmetic now uses `checked_add`, returning `BitError::Eof` on overflow, matching the existing truncation behaviour.
- Same file: two new tests — `length_prefixed_rejects_bad_length_size` (widths 0, 5 and `usize::MAX` return `InvalidLengthSize`) and `length_prefixed_widths` (1-, 2- and 3-byte prefixes split correctly; truncated prefix/payload return `Eof`; empty input yields no NALs). No behaviour change for valid inputs.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-video` — 95 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; doc-tests: 1 passed
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-video bitstream::` — 10 passed, 0 failed, including both new tests
- `cargo fmt -p soundcraft-video -- --check` — clean
- The full workspace test suite was not run; the change is confined to the `soundcraft-video` crate, whose tests pass as above.

title: Open a plugin when it's inserted (#486)
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
Fixes #486

### What changed

Picking a plugin for an insert slot added it but opened nothing, so every new plugin took an extra click on its slot. As in other DAWs, the pick now opens it:

- A hosted plugin (CLAP, VST3, AU) opens its own editor.
- Otherwise its plugin window opens, as a click on the slot does: built-in plugins, no audio engine, or an editor that can't open here (CLAP plugins with only an embedded editor on macOS, #485; Audio Units, #501). The reason is shown in the status line.

title: feat(midi): implement hardware MIDI I/O, live auditioning, and recording
author: Goldwaterfung
body:
Resolves **Gap G-02 (MIDI Hardware Devices)**, providing full clean-room physical MIDI hardware I/O, low-latency live instrument auditioning, and sample-accurate take recording across macOS (CoreMIDI), Windows (WinMM), and Linux (ALSA).

1. Hardware Abstraction & Lock-Free SPSC Queuing (`crates/playback`)
- Integrated `midir` for cross-platform physical device discovery and input stream polling.
- Implemented `LiveMidiEvent` 16-byte zero-allocation POD message representation.
- Designed `MidiInputRing` (bounded lock-free SPSC ring with `Slot` padded to 64 bytes to eliminate cache-line false sharing).
- Implemented `MidiManager` supporting hot-plug rescanning, persistent port enabling via `session.edit.flags`, and dynamic stream synchronization without tearing down existing active connections.

2. Real-Time Audio Callback & Sub-Sample Timing (`crates/playback`, `crates/mix`)
- **Real-Time Safety:** Guaranteed zero heap allocations on the audio thread. Pre-allocated bounded arrays (`[Option<LiveMidiEvent>; 256]`) for block ingestion.
- **Clock Epoch Synchronization:** Hardware callback timestamps are normalized against monotonic host time to eliminate CoreMIDI boot-time epoch mismatches.
- **Clock Jitter Elimination:** `block_start_us` is derived mathematically on the audio thread via rendered sample counts (`rendered_samples * 1_000_000 / sample_rate`), eliminating non-deterministic `Instant::now()` system calls during steady-state playback.
- **Sub-Sample Accurate Offsetting:** Input events are timestamp-mapped to sample offsets `[0..block_len)` within the audio buffer.

3. Mixer Routing, Voice Tracking & Monitoring (`crates/mix`)
- **Low-Latency Monitoring PDC Bypass:** Monitored/record-armed tracks bypass alignment and extra delay lines (`st.align = 0`, `st.out_extra = 0`), ensuring zero latency for performers.
- **16-Channel Voice Tracking:** Implemented `HeldNotes` using a zero-allocation `[u64; 32]` bitset (2048 distinct (channel, pitch) states). Eliminates cro…

title: fix(playback): retry the next output config when a stream won't start (#440)
author: nanox333
body:
Fixes #440

### What changed

A stream that builds but fails `stream.play()` only logged a warning, and `Player::open` still returned it as operational, so the device was never retried and no fallback ran. Now a failed start is treated like a failed build: that stream is dropped and the next config is tried (the default buffer size after the chosen one), and only then the silent clock.

- `start_stream` returns `false` when `play()` fails.
- The attempt loop in `Player::open` is now `first_started`, which takes the build and start steps as parameters, so the fallback order can be tested without an audio device.
- The success path is unchanged: a stream that starts is used as before.

### Checks

- New tests in `soundcraft-playback`: a stream that won't start is reported as failed; the first config that starts wins and later ones aren't tried; a config that fails to build falls through; no startable config yields `None`, which leads to the silent clock.
- `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback --lib`: 33 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p soundcraft-playback --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- Not run: the full `cargo xtask ci` gate and the wasm check. The silent-clock branch of `Player::open` is not run by a test; only the helper's `None` result is.

title: Plugin editor windows on Linux (VST3 and embedded CLAP, X11)
author: ayozetr
body:
## Summary

Third-party plugin GUIs now open on **Linux** (and the BSDs). Until now VST3 editors reported `VST3 editors are not hosted on this platform yet` there, and CLAP plugins with only an embedded editor were refused. This follows the Windows work in #315, same structure.

- **VST3** (`soundcraft-vst3-host`): an X11 implementation of the `window` module (`kPlatformTypeX11EmbedWindowID`). The view embeds into a top-level window on our own X11 connection (XWayland on Wayland desktops), sized from `getSize`, resized on `IPlugFrame::resizeView`, with fixed size hints. Closing it only hides it (`WM_DELETE_WINDOW`); the editor link's `idle` then detaches the view and destroys the window, as on macOS/Windows.
- **VST3 run loop**: X11 editors have no event loop of their own, so `PlugFrame` also implements `Linux::IRunLoop`. Plugins register their display connection's fd and their repaint timers; the editor link's `idle` (once per UI frame, which is every 30 ms while an editor is open) polls the fds without blocking and fires due timers. Without this, JUCE editors open but never repaint.
- **CLAP** (`soundcraft-clap-host`): embedded-only editors get the same X11 host window (`create(x11, false)` → `get_size` → `set_parent` → `show`, `request_resize` applied in `idle`). The host now offers `clap.timer-support` and `clap.posix-fd-support` on X11, kept per instance and serviced by the editor's `idle`; registrations are dropped when the instance goes. Floating X11 editors benefit from these too.
- Everything stays inside each crate's `ffi.rs` (`unsafe` only there, `// SAFETY:` on every block). New Linux/BSD-only dependencies: `x11rb` 0.13 (pure Rust, already in the lockfile through winit) and `libc` (zero-timeout `poll`). Callbacks never run with the run-loop lock held, so plugins can (un)register from inside them; one removed earlier in the same pass is skipped.

title: Undo is for edits: solo, mute, record and view settings aren't undo steps (#492)
author: mikkelkonyher
body:
Fixes #492

### What changed

Cmd+Z undid Solo, Mute, Record Enable, track height and view, group activation and insert bypass. Soloing a track and pressing Cmd+Z to undo the last edit took back the solo instead, and every solo, mute or record-arm press filled the history. As in Pro Tools, Logic and Ableton, undo is now for edits:

- The commands listed in #492 are `noundo`: `mix.solo`, `mix.mute`, `mix.solo_safe`, `mix.clear_solos`, `mix.clear_mutes`, `mix.record_arm`, `mix.input_monitor`, `track.set_record_to_input_only`, `track.height` (+ `_up`/`_down`), `track.view`, `track.hide`, `track.change_width`, `track.group_toggle`, `mix.automation_mode`, `mix.insert_bypass` and `track.bypass_*`.
- `track.pin` and `track.color` stay undoable, as in Pro Tools.
- They're still journaled, and the session is still marked modified when they change, since they're saved with it.

How: undo restores a whole-document snapshot, so marking them `noundo` alone would put the old solo, mute, height and so on back on the next Cmd+Z. Each history entry now also keeps the document right after its step (an `Arc`), and `Engine::keep_live_state` carries what changed since then over to the restored snapshot, next to `keep_edit_mode`. What the edit itself changed is still undone: undoing a track preset takes its mute back, and undoing Commit shows the original track again. Insert bypass carries over only where the slot still holds the same plugin, and a width change carries its panners with it.

`docs/architecture.md` says a `noundo` command that changes the document needs its fields carried over in `keep_live_state`. `docs/mcp.md` and the Undo/redo row in `docs/target-app-parity.md` are updated.

These used one of the settings as an example undo step:

- `track_height`: the two height-drag tests checked that a drag is one undo step. They now check that it isn't an undo step at all. This is the one behavior change to an existing test worth a look.

author: LabDennis

title: fix(audio-io): poison stream encoders after a failed write so later calls cannot claim success (#464)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #464

## Summary

The stream encoders (`FileEncoder` for WAV, AIFF and FLAC) stayed usable after a write failed partway through a block. `write_all` can append a prefix of the block before reporting the error, but the WAV/AIFF writers only advance their frame counter after a fully successful write, and the FLAC writer clears the pending samples before writing the encoded frame. A caller that continued after such an error could call `finish` successfully and get back headers whose counts disagree with the bytes actually on the sink — or, for FLAC, a stream that silently lost a frame of audio.

Each writer now poisons itself on the first failed block/frame write: every later `write` and `finish` call fails with an encode error instead of completing an inconsistent file. Refusals that happen before anything is written (the format size limits checked by `check_room`) do not poison the encoder, and encoders that never see a failed write behave exactly as before.

## Changes

- `crates/audio-io/src/lib.rs` — shared `failed_write_error()` for the poisoned state, and a note on `FileEncoder::write` documenting that a failed write makes the encoder unusable.
- `crates/audio-io/src/wav.rs` — `Writer` records a failed `write_interleaved` call and refuses later `write`/`finish`.
- `crates/audio-io/src/aiff.rs` — same poisoning for the AIFF writer.
- `crates/audio-io/src/flac.rs` — same poisoning when a frame write fails (the case that also lost the frame's samples).
- `crates/audio-io/tests/stream.rs` — regression test with a sink that accepts a 256-byte prefix and then fails every write: across WAV, AIFF and FLAC, the first `write` errors and both a later `write` and `finish` return an error instead of claiming success.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-audio-io` — all suites pass, including the new `a_failed_write_poisons_the_encoder` regression test and the existing stream tests (streamed output still matches whole-buffer encodes byte for byte; format-limit refusal…

title: Preserve selection gaps and automation when duplicating or repeating
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Duplicate and Repeat now capture the original arrangement once and prepare one bounded plan before editing. Slip replaces the entire destination, including silence; Shuffle inserts the aggregate duration once while preserving locked barriers and their later material, and refuses an insertion inside a crossfade or without enough room. Automation Follows Edit copies original curves, and fresh clip IDs retain supported processing metadata and MIDI performances.

The three existing commands share this feature implementation. Successful operations use one Undo step; unsupported or malformed selections fail before changing the document or clipboard. Musical placement is limited to exactly representable constant-tempo boundaries with equal sample widths. Processed partial material, note-only editing, locked/grouped material that would be edited and touched loop identities remain explicitly unsupported.

This is the standalone Selection Repeat split requested in #394. It contains no runtime rewrite, originals store, delivery changes or repository-wide governance rules. Other integration review findings remain separate work.

Validation: the unchanged full isolated Linux `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` passed all six gates (format, Clippy, tests, assets, layers and WASM): 1,071 tests passed, zero failed, one existing ignored and zero filtered. Focused preflight separately passed all 19 Selection Repeat cases, 41 existing edit/command cases and all 27 existing edit-mode cases. Existing tests and fixtures remain unchanged.

title: Read bus-send pan and mute automation
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Bus sends read pan automation for mono-to-stereo routes and mute automation for ordinary bus formats. Valid reading-mode lanes override their static controls; missing, empty, malformed and Off-mode lanes retain static behavior. Stereo sends retain existing left/right routing even when stored static pan is nonzero.

The new send readers use the timeline represented by the selected audio buffer for both cursor initialization and per-frame lookup. Audio taps include processor-declared insert delay and actual applied alignment. Insert age is accumulated independently of the mixer’s bounded delay-compensation field. Aux taps also include known upstream bus ages; their pre-fader copies and aligned post-fader buffers use their own delays. Nested known paths propagate that metadata. Later output, receiving-processor and Master delays do not move a source send's clock.

The regressions confirm the review's unrelated silent Maximizer case is corrected: a mute at frame 300 leaves sample 299 audible after offline latency removal. Audio samples, routing matrices, delay-line placement, offline latency removal and the older send-level/control schedules retain their existing behavior. Mixed-age bus sums have no single source timeline and retain the earlier render-position clock; complete graph delay compensation remains separate.

The helper paths use local cursors and fixed metadata without adding a dynamic collection. Lane validity still scans points once per callback; whole-mixer allocation freedom, realtime deadlines and physical-device behavior remain unmeasured. Automated stereo pan, ambisonic and non-bus automation, writing/safing and global automation policy remain separate.

Validation on isolated Linux, before publication:

- The exact six latency fixtures against the previous head produced five expected behavioral failures; the mixed-age fallback fixture passed.

title: Bounce: a Dither option in the dialog and for stems (#522)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #522

Every 16- and 24-bit bounce was TPDF-dithered with no way to turn it off: the Bounce dialog never sent `dither` (so `file.bounce_mix` used its default, `true`), and `file.bounce_stems` hard-coded `dither: true`.

## Change

- **Bounce dialog:** a **Dither (TPDF)** checkbox under Normalize, **off by default** as the issue asks (Pro Tools behaviour: the master chain decides). It's disabled for 32-bit float, where there's nothing to dither, and the dialog then sends `dither: false`.
- **`file.bounce_stems`** takes `dither?: true`, like `file.bounce_mix`.
- The engine defaults stay `true`, so scripts and MCP callers that don't pass `dither` keep today's output.
- README: "with optional dither".

**User-visible:** a 16/24-bit bounce from the dialog is now undithered unless Dither is ticked.

`soundcraft-cli convert` always dithering is a separate issue (#548) and is not touched here.

## Tests

- `crates/ui-egui/tests/bounce.rs`: `the_bounce_dialog_dithers_only_when_dither_is_ticked`. The dialog opens with Dither off; a 16-bit bounce without it is within ½ LSB of the 32-bit float bounce on every sample, and ticking Dither moves samples further. The test doesn't compile on `main` (no `dither` field).
- `crates/engine/src/io.rs`: `stems_dither_only_when_asked`, the same check for `file.bounce_stems` with `dither: false` against the default. Fails on `main`.
- Locally: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, assets and layers. The wasm step was not run: Gentoo's Rust ships no `wasm32-unknown-unknown` std. CI covers it.
- On this machine, `autosave::tests::saved_audio_is_referenced_and_takes_are_copied_once` and some tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/recovery.rs` fail intermittently. They fail the same way on an untouched `main` (c0cb993) and aren't related to this change.

title: cli: reject unknown options and missing option values
author: Hamza0101
body:
Fixes #549

### The problem

`convert`, `run` and `script` read options with `arg_value`, which matches a flag exactly and takes the argument after it:

```rust
args.iter().position(|a| a == flag).and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned()
```

A misspelling, an `--option=value` form, or an option with its value missing therefore all read as **absent**, and nothing inspects what is left over. The command ran without what was asked for and still exited 0.

Reproduced on `c0cb993`, the commit named in the issue, with a 0.1 s 48 kHz 16-bit tone:

| command | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `convert … --rate 44100` | 44100 Hz | 44100 Hz (unchanged) |
| `convert … --rate` | exit 0, 48000 Hz | exit 1, `--rate needs a value` |
| `convert … --rate=44100` | exit 0, 48000 Hz | exit 0, 44100 Hz |
| `convert … --bitdepth 16` | exit 0, Int24 | exit 1, `unknown option --bitdepth` |
| `convert … --bit-depth=16` | exit 0, Int24 | exit 0, Int16 |
| `convert … --normalise` | exit 0, un-normalised | exit 1, `unknown option --normalise` |
| `convert … --bogus` | exit 0, file written | exit 1, `unknown option --bogus` |
| `run --cmd session.new --bounce` | exit 0, no file | exit 1, `--bounce needs a value` |
| `run … --bounces x.wav` | exit 0, no file | exit 1, `unknown option --bounces` |
| `run … --bounce=y.wav` | exit 0, no file | exit 0, `y.wav` written |

### The change

`check_options` takes the options a subcommand accepts, with whether each carries a value, and rejects an unknown option or a missing value. `arg_value` additionally reads `--option=value`, which the issue called a bonus and which makes the forms people evidently reach for do what they look like.

Applied to `convert`, `run` and `script`. `script` is included because it shares `--in`, `--demo`, `--save` and `--bounce` with `run` through `load_engine` and `finish`, so validating one and not the other would leave the same flags checked in one place and not the other.

`app` and `mcp` are left alone: both parse arg…

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `soundcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon alsa-lib vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: soundcraft`;
  - `conflicts: soundcraft, soundcraft-bin, soundcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.soundcraft`, not `soundcraft`.** The AUR already has `soundcraft`, `soundcraft-bin` and `soundcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing

- I ran `package.sh --skip-build --formats arch` with the binaries from the published v0.6.1 x86_64 tarball, checked against `SHA256SUMS.txt`. It produced `soundcraft-0.6.1-linux-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst`.

title: convert: dither only when the output loses resolution (#548)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #548

`soundcraft-cli convert` passed `dither: true` for every conversion, so a same-depth or wider conversion still added ±1 LSB TPDF noise, and digital silence came out as noise.

## What changes

- `convert` now dithers only when it writes integer samples that cannot hold the source exactly:
  - the output has fewer bits than the source (24 to 16-bit),
  - the source is float or a lossy codec (or 32-bit integer, which is already rounded to f32 on decode),
  - `--rate` (to a different rate) or `--normalize` produced new sample values.
- 32-bit float output never dithers.
- A 16-bit file written as 16 or 24-bit, or anything written as 32f, is copied sample for sample, and digital silence stays silent.
- `--dither` and `--no-dither` override the automatic choice; both together are an error (exit 1). This follows the Dither option that #551 adds to Bounce (#522), which does not cover `convert`.
- Usage text and ROADMAP progress log updated.

User-visible: conversions that keep or widen the bit depth no longer change the samples (previously ~25% of samples moved by 1 LSB); conversions that reduce depth behave as before.

## Tests

- Unit tests for the flag parsing and the automatic decision (`auto_dither`).
- `apps/soundcraft-cli/tests/convert.rs` runs the real binary: silence and a 16-bit tone converted to 16, 24 (also the default) and 32f come back unchanged; `--dither` still dithers; a 24-bit source with sub-LSB detail is dithered to 16-bit by default and rounded with `--no-dither`. Both tests fail on main.

`cargo xtask ci` locally: fmt, clippy, assets and layers pass; `cargo test --workspace` passes except `soundcraft-ui-egui --test recovery` (3 autosave-recovery tests), which fail the same way on an unmodified main checkout on this machine, so they are environmental and unrelated. The wasm step was not run: Gentoo's Rust has no wasm32 std.

title: Lossless audio: keep timing and report damage instead of silently dropping frames (#550)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #550

A damaged FLAC decoded silently to shorter audio: the FLAC demuxer drops a frame whose checksum fails and resyncs on the next one (so the `DecodeError` branch in `symph.rs` never even saw it), all later audio moved one block earlier, and a truncated file just stopped. `convert` and `file.import_audio` reported success.

## What changes

- `soundcraft-audio-io`, lossless streams only (lossy codecs keep skipping bad packets as before):
  - a FLAC frame the demuxer dropped is found from the gap in the packet timestamps and filled with silence of the same length, never past the length the file declares;
  - a packet that fails to decode is likewise replaced by silence of its duration;
  - `AudioInfo` gains `damage: Option<String>` (serde default, skipped when `None`), describing corrupt frames, a demux error, or audio that ends before its declared length. `probe` leaves it `None` (it does not decode).
- `soundcraft-cli convert` refuses a damaged file: exit 1, `damaged audio, nothing written: …` on stderr, no output file.
- `file.import_audio` still imports it (the timing now holds), logs a warning and adds a `warning` field to that file's entry in the result.
- ROADMAP progress log.

User-visible: `convert` of a damaged or truncated lossless file now fails instead of writing shorter audio; importing one keeps later audio in place (silence where the frame was lost) and returns a warning. Intact files are unaffected.

## Tests

- `crates/audio-io/tests/damage.rs`: an intact FLAC reports no damage; with one byte flipped mid-file, the decode is still 48000 frames, every sample is either the original at the same position or silence, and the damage is reported; a FLAC cut in half is reported as ending early; WAV/AIFF report none.

title: Retain encoded originals for native audio imports
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Native audio import currently keeps decoded working audio but loses opaque container bytes when it writes derived media. This change retains the exact encoded import separately, publishes it in native session folders, and verifies it on Open and copy boundaries.

Temporary assets follow document/history/snapshot leases and are collected after the last lease expires. On Unix, temporary capture directories and files are created owner-only (0700 and 0600) before encoded bytes are written. Ordinary Save uses a verified identity/metadata receipt to avoid rehashing unchanged published originals. The existing decode, rate conversion, placement and playback paths stay in use.

This is the originals store split requested in #394. It addresses temporary cleanup, repeated Save hashing and normal package-test execution. Browser/bundle retention and the mix/playback rewrite are outside this PR; original-bearing bundles fail explicitly rather than omit data. Missing originals retain diagnostics/receipts and block incomplete saves. Metadata caching assumes accurate filesystem stamps, and project save retains its existing per-file failure behavior.

Validation: the exact candidate passed the unchanged `cargo +1.95.0 xtask ci` gate on isolated Linux (format, Clippy, workspace tests, assets, layers and WASM), with 1,070 workspace tests passed, zero failed, one existing ignored and zero filtered. All 17 tracked regression cases passed, covering independent encoded-byte/PCM expectations, save/open/copy, snapshot cleanup, replacement-file protection, confinement, legacy sessions, explicit bundle refusal, and owner-only creation under umask 022. The permissions case checks empty and mid-write files, exclusive creation and snapshot cleanup. No UI source changed.

title: Keep deep Aux and Folder routing chains in dependency order
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Deep Aux and Folder chains can lose audio when downstream returns are created before their producers: the current routing-depth calculation caps every path at eight, so deep producers and consumers tie.

Compile exact longest-path depths for acyclic Aux/Folder graphs when the existing structure fingerprint changes. Output and send dependencies count each producer once per destination; strips at equal depth retain session order. Any cycle retains the existing bounded ordering for the whole graph.

This is one routing-order increment of the remaining runtime work in #394. It preserves current PDC, plugin processing/failure containment, routing coefficients, renderer APIs and playback/device ownership. Other runtime changes remain separate.

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

SoundCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`, `alsa-lib`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with

storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

title: Apply the punch range before placing a recorded take
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #431

## Cause
`place_recording` placed the whole take with `add_recording` first and trimmed to the punch range afterwards. Placing the full take cleared the existing material across the pre-roll and post-roll, and trimming could not bring it back.

## Fix
The punch range is now applied inside `add_recording_in`, before placement. The clip's start, length and source offset are cut to the punch range, so only the punched span is overwritten. A pass that falls entirely outside the punch range is skipped and creates no clip or playlist. `place_recording` no longer needs the separate trim step.

## Verified
- Regression test `punching_in_keeps_the_material_around_the_punch_range`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib punching_in_keeps_the_material_around_the_punch_range`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Recording without a punch range goes through the original placement path with the same start, length and source offset. `add_recording` keeps its signature.

title: Plugin scans in the background, cached between launches; Setup > Plug-in Folders
author: Limestudio90
body:
## Problem

Hovering **CLAP** or **VST3** in a Mix insert or instrument menu scanned the plugin folders on the UI thread. The app froze until every plugin file had loaded, and that happened again at every launch. On my machine it took 5.4 s for 17 VST3s, and 4.8 s of that was one plugin (Supertone Clear) loading its model.

## What changes

- **Scans no longer block the UI.** The VST3 and CLAP registries now scan without holding their lock. A separate lock still runs scans one at a time. While files load, the UI can read the cached list and plugin infos, and a plugin is created from the previous or cached list rather than waiting for the scan.
- **Each new plugin file is loaded in a child process.** The app runs `<its own program> --scan-vst3|--scan-clap <file>`, which prints one marked JSON line and exits. A crash, a timeout (120 s) or unreadable output is recorded as that file's failure.
  - Why: loading a library in-process holds the OS loader lock while its initialisers run. On Windows that stalled every other thread that loaded a library or started one, so at a cold launch the window stayed **black for 7 s** while Clear initialised. dyld (macOS) and glibc (Linux) hold a similar lock while initialisers run.
  - A plugin that crashes while loading now takes only the child down.
  - Plugins are loaded into the app only when first used, on the main thread, as before.
- **Cache between launches (like REAPER).** `plugins-vst3.json` and `plugins-clap.json` in the settings folder record what each plugin file held, keyed by the size and modification time of its binary. A scan loads only new and changed files. A file that failed to load is not retried until it changes. `rescan()` still loads everything.
- **Background scan at launch.** The app starts the scan when it opens. The CLAP/VST3 submenus read the cached list and show a spinner with "Scanning…" until it is ready.

title: Mix: Alt-click sets an input or output on every track, Alt+Shift on the selected ones, Cmd cascades the inputs (#570)
author: Testsubject1337
body:
Closes #570.

Setting up a session meant opening each strip's input menu in turn. The Mix window's I/O menus now read the modifiers on the click, as in Pro Tools:

- **Alt (Option)-click**: every track that has the connection gets it (audio and aux tracks for inputs; those and instrument tracks for outputs).
- **Alt+Shift-click**: the selected tracks get it.
- **With Cmd (Ctrl) held as well**, a hardware input **cascades**: the clicked track gets the chosen input and each next track the channels after it, a stereo track taking two (`In 3`, `In 4-5`, `In 6`, …).
- A hint line at the bottom of the menu says so, with the platform's modifier names.

The cascade is the engine's: `track.input` takes `cascade: true` with an `In N` input and assigns the run over its tracks, so the CLI, the control channel and MCP can do it too, and the whole assignment is one command and one undo step. title: Fix stale sample read at the end of each mix block when device and session rates differ
author: DCubix
body:
## Problem

When the device sample rate differs from the session rate (for example a 44.1 kHz
device with a 48 kHz session), the output resampler in `AudioState::fill`
interpolates between `pending[c][i0]` and `pending[c][i0 + 1]`.

`pending` is `BLOCK` (512) samples long, but only the first `pending_len` samples
belong to the current block. When `i0 + 1 == pending_len`, the second sample is
leftover data from an earlier block. The result is one small discontinuity at the
end of every mix block. It is audible as crackling.

At equal rates the fractional part is 0, so the bug does not appear.
Lower buffer sizes make the mix block (`quantum`) smaller, so there are more block
edges per second and the crackling is louder.

## Change

At the block edge, use the last valid sample for the second interpolation point
instead of reading past `pending_len`.

This holds the last sample for the final fraction of a block. It is a deliberate
simplification, noted in a code comment. Carrying the first sample of the
next block would be exact, but needs the next block to be rendered first.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p soundcraft-playback`: passes.
- Tested on hardware with a 44.1 kHz device and a 48 kHz session. Before/after
  videos are attached below.
- No automated test covers the block edge.

### Before
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73110701-a994-469a-9a80-392c32c211f0

### After
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/695fb95a-c8cf-48c3-86ef-7605a7227402


## Related

- #490 fixes the input monitoring ring. It is independent of this change.

title: Saturate midi.notes_move tick and pitch arithmetic
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/midi.rs:129-130` (no existing issue): midi.notes_move overflows (panics) on huge `ticks` or `semitones`.

## Cause
`notes_move` added the unclamped `ticks` and `semitones` command params to a note's start and pitch with plain `+`. With `i64::MAX` this overflows. Debug builds panic, which `Engine::execute` reports as `EngineError::Internal`. Release builds wrap silently, so a huge positive `ticks` sent the note to the clip start.

## Fix
Both sums now use `saturating_add`. The existing `.max(0)` on the start and `.clamp(0, 127)` on the pitch are unchanged. A huge move now pushes the note to the far right, or pins the pitch at 127, without an error.

## Verified
- Regression test `notes_move_huge_params_do_not_overflow`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib notes_move_huge_params_do_not_overflow`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change the other midi commands or add a range limit on `ticks` or `semitones`.

title: Reject invalid send slot in automation.copy_to_send
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/cmd/mix.rs:697` (no existing issue): automation.copy_to_send silently writes to Send A when `send` is invalid.

## Cause
`copy_to_send` parsed `send` with `slot_of(...).unwrap_or(0)`. An out-of-range, unparseable or missing slot became slot 0. The command then copied volume automation into the Send A level lane and recorded an undo step.

## Fix
`copy_to_send` now returns a BadParams error when `send` is missing or not a valid slot (0..N or a..x). That matches the behaviour of `mix.send_remove` and `mix.insert`. Nothing is edited and no undo step is pushed on error.

## Verified
- Regression test `copy_to_send_rejects_an_invalid_send_slot`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-engine --lib copy_to_send_rejects`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The copy logic for valid slots is unchanged. `slot_of` and the other slot-taking commands are unchanged.

title: Reuse send channel-conversion coefficients between blocks
author: ProdByBuddha
body:
Bus sends reconstruct channel-conversion coefficients on every rendered block. Reuse one boxed matrix per nominal send slot while its effective format, width, pan law and resolved pan values are unchanged; refresh coefficients in place when those inputs change.

The pointer table stays bounded, and extra send slots retain the original uncached conversion. Destination lookup, gain, mute and pre/post source selection remain live. Mono sends retain their own pan, stereo sends retain hard left/right routing, and explicit surround settings retain precedence over following the track.

First eligible use may allocate on the render owner; no off-callback preparation or measured latency gain is claimed. Output conversion, Aux inputs, routing order, plugins, PDC, renderer interfaces and playback/device ownership remain separate.

title: video: budget coded pixel geometry before decoding
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Fixes #427. The pixel budget was enforced only after a frame was decoded (`Movie`), while allocations are sized from the codec's coded geometry: a crafted ProRes frame header (16-bit width/height, up to 65535x65535 pixels) or an H.264 SPS (up to 1024x1024 macroblocks per axis) inside a container whose own dimensions pass the opening check could drive multi-gigabyte allocations, ending in an allocation-failure abort.

The shared `MAX_PIXELS` budget (8192x8192) now lives at the crate root and is checked on coded geometry before anything is allocated — in `prores::decode_frame_into` right after the frame header is parsed, and beside the existing per-dimension cap in `Sps::parse`; `Movie`'s post-decode checks stay as a backstop. Regression tests craft an over-budget ProRes header (refused with `picture too large` before the planes; 8192x8192 at the budget still proceeds) and an over-budget SPS via the existing test writer (refused; exactly-at-budget 8192x8192 still parses); both fail on the unpatched code. `cargo test -p soundcraft-video --lib` passes (96 passed, 0 failed).

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: session: reject duplicate ids and an exhausted id space on load
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Fixes #448. `Session::from_json` accepted documents with duplicate ids in a namespace and with saturated allocator state, so after loading, commands, selections and source associations could act on an arbitrary one of two objects sharing an id, and every further allocation returned `u64::MAX` again.

A new `Session::validate`, run after `sanitize`, rejects duplicate track/clip/source/video/bus/marker/group ids — the error names the namespace and the repeated id — and rejects an exhausted id space (`next_id` or any existing id at `u64::MAX`, which `sanitize` folds into `next_id`). Sessions written by SoundCraft itself never contain either, so only crafted or corrupted files are affected. Regression tests load a session with two tracks sharing an id and sessions with a maximal `next_id` / maximal existing id, asserting `SessionError::Invalid`; all fail without the new call (the sessions load `Ok`) and `cargo test -p soundcraft-model --lib` passes (37 passed, 0 failed).

Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: Round negative timecode and feet+frames positions symmetrically
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/timecode.rs:111` (no existing issue): Negative timecode and feet+frames positions parse one sample off (asymmetric rounding in FrameRate::samples_at_frame).

## Cause
`FrameRate::samples_at_frame` added `n/2` and then used truncating integer division. That rounds half up for positive frames, but for negative frames truncation toward zero rounds the other way. At 25 fps and 48 kHz, `-00:00:01:00` parsed to -47999 instead of -48000, so format→parse was not a round trip.

## Fix
`samples_at_frame` now rounds the magnitude of the frame count half away from zero and reapplies the sign. Negative frames therefore mirror positive ones. Timecode, Feet+Frames and `position_param` parsing all go through this function, so all three are fixed. Two regression tests were added: one in `timecode.rs` and one in `format.rs`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `timecode::tests::negative_timecode_rounds_symmetrically`, `format::tests::parse_round_trips_timecode_negative`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-time --lib -- negative_timecode_rounds_symmetrically parse_round_trips_timecode_negative`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`frames_at` (already floors with `div_euclid`), the other time formats, and the behaviour for non-negative frames are unchanged.

title: Fix Min:Secs showing 1 ms early at exact millisecond positions
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/format.rs:46` (no existing issue): Min:Secs counter/ruler shows 1 ms too early at exact millisecond positions (44.1 kHz) because of float floor.

## Cause
`min_secs` computed `(seconds * 1000.0).floor()` in floating point. Exact millisecond positions, such as sample 88641 at 44.1 kHz, come out just below the integer, so floor shows one millisecond too little (`0:02.009` instead of `0:02.010`).

## Fix
`min_secs` now computes whole milliseconds in integer arithmetic, `|s| * 1000 / hz` in i128. The mins/secs/ms split is the same as before. The result saturates instead of overflowing.

## Verified
- Regression tests `known_positions_at_44100`, `negative_position_at_44100`, `every_exact_millisecond_displays_exactly`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p soundcraft-time --test min_secs_exact_ms`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The Min:Secs parser, the other timebases, and `SampleRate::seconds` are unchanged.

title: packaging: sign macOS binaries with the plug-in-hosting entitlement (#153)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
With only the microphone entitlement, hardened runtime's library validation refused every third-party VST3/CLAP/AU binary signed by another team, so a release build scanned no plug-ins (the reported log line: "mapping process and mapped file (non-platform) have different Team IDs"). This adds `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation` to the macOS entitlements and signs the CLI with the same entitlements file, since the CLI hosts plug-ins in-process too.
